jobs.description:
Very Big Things · Remote · Eastern Time ±2 hours preferred · South Florida a plus · Reports to the CEO

ABOUT VERY BIG THINGS

Very Big Things is an enterprise AI transformation company headquartered in Fort Lauderdale. We help large companies adopt AI successfully at scale by redesigning critical workflows and building AI directly into the work. We do that through Transform Work, our engagement model; SHIM, the open-source methodology we created; and TrackFrame, the platform backbone beneath the workflows we build. Our clients range from PE-backed mid-market companies to Fortune 100 enterprises, and we have grand ambitions for growth. That’s where you come in.

JOB PURPOSE

VBT has a documented go-to-market strategy, a set of committed bets, and a senior team with deep relationships and real deal flow. What it needs is an operator: the person who turns strategy into a weekly operating rhythm and keeps it running at full pressure.

You will own the go-to-market operating system end-to-end: the cadence, the scorecard, the pipeline hygiene, and the execution of each bet, working with the team members who own relationships and revenue.

The CEO currently carries much of this. Your job is to take it off his plate and build a machine that no longer depends on him to keep it running.

Success looks like: bets executed on cadence, a dashboard the whole team trusts, and a steady, measurable flow of qualified conversations that become revenue-generating client relationships.

To be successful in this role, you need a bias for action. Ideas are not the constraint; consistent execution is. You should be energized by turning a plan into owners, dates, fields and dashboards, then relentlessly making sure all of it gets done with autonomy and agency.

This starts as a highly hands-on operating role, but the mandate is bigger than maintaining the current system. As VBT grows, you will help build and ultimately lead the GTM operations function around it.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Run the GTM operating rhythm: own the weekly go-to-market meeting, deal reviews, and a scorecard review cadence that drives decisions.
  • Own the scorecard: define and track the leading indicators for every live bet, including qualified conversations, second meetings inside 14 days, partner-sourced briefs, room and event outcomes, and make HubSpot the single source of truth the team actually trusts.
  • Operationalize the bets: for each committed motion, including relationship re-engagement, partner and reseller enablement, executive events, consultant strategy, and demand generation marketing, ensure there is an owner, a backup, next actions with dates, and follow-up sequences that run to completion. Seven or eight touches, not one.
  • Own the executive event production line: including vendor management for audience generation and syndication, pre-booked 1:1 meeting management, and post-event follow-up outreach.
  • Run the consultant channel operating system: own briefing materials, touch cadence, brief intake and attribution. Senior leadership owns the relationships; this role makes sure the channel actually operates.
  • Manage the partner operating cadence: keep relationships with ServiceNow, AWS, resellers, and other strategic partners moving through enablement materials, deal registration, standing presence at partner sales meetings, certification and program requirements, and consistent follow-through.
  • Run trigger intelligence: maintain the account list and the signals that time our outreach, including new executive mandates, stalled AI pilots, funding and regulatory events, and turn them into a weekly call order for the revenue team.
  • Own GTM tooling and data hygiene: required fields, source attribution from day one, meeting grading, workflows, automation, and the reporting the CEO and leadership team use to run the business.
  • Build the GTM operations function as VBT scales: determine where internal hires, agencies, fractional resources, technology, and automation are needed, and ultimately manage the people and resources responsible for running the system.
  • Coordinate marketing execution: manage the fractional, agency, and internal resources behind our media, content, and events programs and connect their output to pipeline. Support case study content production and award programs.
  • Prepare the weekly leadership view: what’s working, what’s stalled, what gets cut, and what should change. Bring a recommendation, not just a report.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • 6–8+ years in revenue operations, GTM operations, or growth/business operations for a B2B services, consultancy, or agency business, ideally one selling complex work into mid-market and enterprise clients. Exceptional candidates with less traditional experience but a strong track record of operating at this level are welcome.
  • Proven experience running an operating cadence for a revenue team: pipeline reviews, scorecards, and QBR-style reporting that leadership actually used.
  • Experience running partner or consultant channels to generate pipeline.
  • Hands-on HubSpot fluency, or equivalent CRM experience at an admin level: fields, workflows, sequences, attribution, dashboards.
  • Experience working directly with a founder or CEO: comfortable taking a system off their plate, disagreeing constructively, and holding senior colleagues to commitments without owning them hierarchically.
  • An operator’s temperament: organized, persistent, detail-oriented, and allergic to loose ends. You’d rather close eight loops than open eight new ones.
  • Genuine curiosity about AI and the ability to learn quickly. You do not need to arrive as an expert in enterprise AI transformation, but you should be interested enough in the space to become fluent over time and eventually speak credibly about what we do and why it matters.
  • An AI-native approach to your own work: actively looking for ways to use AI and automation to improve research, reporting, follow-up, analysis, and GTM execution.
  • Comfort with a small, fast, remote-first team where the playbook exists but the machine is still being assembled.

HOW THIS ROLE IS JUDGED

First 90 days: the operating cadence is running and respected; the scorecard is live with agreed definitions of “qualified”; every committed bet has an owner, a backup, and current next actions; the dashboard is trusted enough that leadership decisions cite it.

Ongoing: leading indicators trend up quarter over quarter, follow-up sequences complete rather than stall, the GTM operations function gets stronger as the company scales, and the CEO spends his go-to-market time in rooms with clients rather than running the machine.

POSITION DETAILS

This is a full-time position.

Remote. Candidates located within roughly two hours of Eastern Time are preferred. South Florida is a plus given our client, partner, and leadership footprint, but we will prioritize exceptional talent over location.

A Moving Experience.

Who is Cerence AI?

Cerence AI is the global leader in AI for transportation, specialized in building AI and voice-powered companions for cars, two-wheelers, and more that enable people to focus on what matters most. With over 500 million cars shipped with Cerence AI's technology, we partner with leading automakers (such as Volkswagen, Mercedes, Audi, Toyota and many more), mobility providers, and technology companies to power intuitive, integrated experiences that create safer, more connected, and more enjoyable journeys for drivers and passengers alike.

Our Driving Force

Our team is dedicated to pushing the boundaries of AI innovation, working around the globe with headquarters in Burlington, Massachusetts, USA and 16 other offices across Europe, Asia, and North America. We bring together diverse backgrounds, and varied skill sets with the shared goal of advancing the next generation of transportation user experiences. Our culture is customer-centric, collaborative, fast-paced, and fun, with continuous opportunities for learning and development to support your career growth.

Interested in having a significant impact in a dynamic industry with a high-performing global team? We’re looking for an exceptional SeniorPrincipalAI Scientist in Generative AI who is ready to drive the future of mobility with us!

What You Will Work On

  • Design and train large‑scale transformer and hybrid foundation models

  • Own model architecture choices across text, multimodal, and emerging paradigms

  • Diagnose and resolve training instabilities at scale

  • Navigate scaling tradeoffs across data, compute, and architecture

  • Define the technical direction for next‑generation models

Core Responsibilities

Deep Learning & Transformer Foundations

  • Apply strong fundamentals in deep learning and representation learning

  • Design and modify transformer architectures, including:

  • Attention variants

  • RoPE, ALiBi

  • Grouped Query Attention (GQA)

  • Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE)

  • Build models from first principles, not just adapt pre‑existing codebases

OptimisationDynamics & Training Stability

  • Own optimizer and scheduler choices, including:

  • AdamW

  • Lion

  • Adafactor

  • Learning‑rate and warmup schedulers

  • Understand and debug:

  • Optimizer instability

  • Gradient pathologies

  • Divergence at large scale

Scaling Laws & Compute Tradeoffs

  • Apply and validate scaling laws

  • Navigate Chinchilla‑style compute vs data tradeoffs

  • Make informed decisions about model size, dataset size, and training duration

Loss Functions & Alignment

  • Design and experiment with loss functions including:

  • Next‑token prediction

  • Contrastive objectives

  • RLHF, DPO, GRPO

  • Understand how loss design impacts convergence, generalization, and alignment

Distributed Foundation Model Training

  • Design and execute large‑scale training using:

  • FSDP

  • ZeRO‑3

  • Tensor parallelism

  • Pipeline parallelism

  • Apply

  • Mixed precision (bf16, fp8)

  • Gradient checkpointing

  • Partner closely with ML systems teams while retaining architectural ownership

Architecture Innovation

  • Explore and implement novel model designs, including:

  • MoE routing strategies

  • Multimodal fusion architectures

  • SSM / hybrid architectures

  • Design architectures with KV cache efficiency and inference implications in mind

What Success Looks Like

  • Training remains stable as models scale in size and complexity

  • Architectural decisions are principled and defensible

  • Models converge faster and generalize better due to architecture and optimisation choices

  • Failure modes are understood, not mysterious

  • The organization develops true in‑house foundation model expertise

Required Experience & Skills

Strongly Required

  • Deep theoretical and practical understanding of modern deep learning

  • Hands‑on experience training large models from scratch

  • Ability to reason about optimization, not just tune hyperparameters

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, research‑driven environments

Critical Technical Skills

  • Transformer internals and attention mechanisms

  • Optimisationalgorithms and training dynamics

  • Scaling laws and compute/data tradeoffs

  • Distributed training strategies and mixed precision

  • Architecture innovation for large, real‑world models

Common Problems You’ll Be Solving

  • Why training diverges at scale

  • How optimizer dynamics interact with architecture

  • When scaling laws break down

  • The real tradeoffs between data, compute, and model design

Availity is seeking a charismatic and accomplished technology leader to join the security leadership team as a Deputy CISO. Areas of focus for this role include Identity Access Management, Risk and Governance, Data Governance, Catastrophic Recovery, and Fraud Prevention. This role sits uniquely in a triangle of leadership reporting to the CISO and partnered with a Deputy CISO whose focus areas include Application Security, Security Operations, and Offensive Security.


Drawing on the appropriate experiences in leadership roles in healthcare information security, the Deputy CISO will be responsible for establishing and maintaining the enterprise vision, strategy, architecture, and a multi-year information security roadmap that assures the company’s information assets and those of its customers are adequately protected. A key element of this role is communicating security at a strategic level to executive management, the Audit and Compliance Board, and the Board of Directors and evangelizing information security across the business to drive adoption of security best practices.

Why work on this team:


  • Lead in a high-profile role that interacts regularly with the Availity’s Board of Directors and C-suite executives
  • Maintain and grow a world-class information security function at an organization operating the nation’s largest healthcare network connecting 2 million providers to every health plan in the US and processes over 13 billion transactions annually
  • Join a forward-thinking team of technology leaders who work together toward the common goal of bettering the overall healthcare system, including collectively navigating an on-prem to cloud migration and leveraging AI and Machine Learning in our SaaS offerings

Requirements:


  • Bachelor's Degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field; (graduate degree preferred).

  • 5+ years of information security/cybersecurity experience
  • Proven experience delivering quality solutions in a SaaS environment

  • Proven experience leading globally diverse teams and working closely with C-suite executives
  • A proven track record in developing information security policies and procedures, and successful execution
  • Extensive knowledge of business risk, risk assessment and risk-based decision making
  • Able to communicate security and risk-related concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences (in business terms), including board level
  • Proven ability to address and present information to a Board of Directors and/or Executive leadership team
  • A natural influencer and coalition builder; passionate about building high performing teams
  • Ability to inspire and motivate cross-functional, interdisciplinary teams to achieve tactical and strategic goals; an innovative leader, problem solver and consultant
  • Ability to evangelize IT security to make it a critical part of business operations; build trust and respect for the security function
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal and collaborative skills
  • Experienced with contract and vendor negotiations
  • Experienced in incident and crisis management with the ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in high-pressure situations
  • Knowledge of security, risk and control frameworks and standards such as HITRUST, ISO 27001 and 27002, SANS-CAG, NIST, FISMA, COBIT, COSO and ITIL
  • Technical acumen including but not limited to: OSI, IT infrastructure, Cloud, application development languages, tools and frameworks, database technologies, web technologies, next gen mobile, network architecture, enterprise architecture, and directory services

  • Professional certifications, such as a CISSP, CISM, CISA
  • Ability to travel 10-15%
  • Healthcare technology industry experience including payer and provider spaces is a plus

What you will be doing:

  • Develop and implement a strategic, long-term information security strategy and roadmap to ensure that Availity’s information assets, and those of its customers under management at Availity, are adequately protected
  • Work with senior leaders across the business to assess and communicate acceptable levels of risk
  • Identify, evaluate and report on information security risks, practices and projects to the Executive Committee and the Board of Directors, and provide subject matter expertise on security standards and best practices e.g. FFIEC, Dodd-Frank, SOX, PCI, etc.
  • Develop, mentor, and manage a high performing staff of information security professionals
  • Develop the Board’s understanding of security beyond a ‘compliance-only’ view
  • Lead the development of up-to-date information security policies, procedures, standards and guidelines, and oversee their approval, dissemination, and maintenance
  • Ensure that the security management program is compliant with applicable laws, regulations, and contractual requirements
  • Act as the champion for the enterprise information security program and foster a security-aware culture
  • Oversee the evaluation, selection and implementation of information security solutions that are innovative, cost-effective, and minimally disruptive
  • Partner with enterprise architects, infrastructure, and applications teams to ensure that technologies are developed and maintained according to security policies and guidelines
  • Manage regular intrusion detection and vulnerability reporting, internal and external IT audit groups reviews, and the coordination of all required fixes
  • Develop business metrics to measure the effectiveness of the security management program, and increase the maturity of the program over time

Job Title

Location(s)

US Remote - MA

Job Description

Scientific Services runs the work around the science so that our customers' scientists do not have to. The practice covers general lab services such as glassware, consumables, PPE, gas management and freezer farms; scientific support such as media and reagent preparation, chemical inventory, scientific shipping and metrology; and technical and analytical work including assay support, cell and tissue culture, purification and instrument-based services such as flow cytometry, LC-MS, NMR, NGS and high-content imaging. It is delivered by specialists embedded in customer laboratories, working to the customer's own SOPs in regulated (GxP) environments.


The Practice Director owns Scientific Services globally as a product. The role defines what the practice sells, why customers buy it, what it costs to deliver, how it is priced and how it evolves, and carries accountability for its revenue, growth and profit.


Owning the product carries two obligations to the rest of the business. The Director enables the commercial organisation to sell it, giving them the proposition, evidence, pricing and confidence to take it to customers. The Director equally enables the operational organisation to deliver it, providing the service design, methodology, standards and capability that make delivery consistent and profitable in every account and region. Alongside this, the Director builds the capability the market will require before it is asked for and represents the organisation as a recognised authority in the field, combining direct leadership of a team of Subject Matter Experts and technical functions with extensive influence across regional, commercial and functional leadership.


Job Responsibilities

  • Own the commercial performance of the practice globally, including revenue, growth and profit. Set the annual plan and the multi-year trajectory, and make the investment, pricing and rationalisation decisions required to deliver them.
  • Define the offering strategy and multi-year roadmap: segments served, offerings to build, scale, partner on or retire, and the position the practice holds against competitors, grounded in market assessment, competitive analysis and customer evidence.
  • Define the customer value proposition, and own the pricing, packaging and rate card architecture together with the business case evidence that supports it.
  • Own service development end to end, taking offerings from concept through design, business case, pilot, launch and hypercare into scaled delivery that is sellable, repeatable and profitable by design.
  • Own go to market and sales enablement, including positioning, qualification criteria, proposal content, pricing guardrails and training, and personally lead the shaping of strategic and complex pursuits.
  • Set and protect the delivery standard through the methodologies, governance, quality frameworks and performance metrics that make delivery consistent in every account and region, with the assurance mechanism to prove it is being met.
  • Build capability ahead of demand, maintaining a forward view of the science, regulation, technology (laboratory automation, informatics and applied AI) and customer operating models, and owning the workforce capability plan and succession for critical expertise.
  • Represent the practice externally as a recognised authority through customer executive forums, industry conferences, publications and strategic partnerships, converting that standing into pipeline and credibility.
  • Recruit, lead and develop a high calibre team of Subject Matter Experts and technical functions, and secure outcomes across regions and functions through influence rather than direct authority.
  • Maintain training and compliance in areas of health and safety, security, environmental and operational aspects of daily activities in the working environment.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities of this job at any time.


Key Relationships

  • Internal. Executive and portfolio leadership, regional and site leadership, other practice leaders, and the commercial, marketing, finance and HR functions.
  • External. Customer scientific, operational and procurement leadership; industry bodies and conference programmes; technology and outsourcing partners.

Critical Skills:

  • Ownership of a services offering, practice or service line with accountability for revenue, growth and margin, at scale and across more than one geography.
  • Offering management discipline applied to services: market assessment, value proposition definition, pricing and packaging, lifecycle management, and build, buy or partner decisions.
  • Deep credibility in scientific and laboratory operations within regulated (GxP) life science environments, with the range to hold both technical and commercial conversations at executive level.
  • Track record of designing and launching new services and scaling them to profitable delivery, supported by methodology, governance and quality frameworks that survived that growth.
  • Influence without authority across a global matrix, and the executive communication to construct and defend an investment case.
  • Recruiting, developing and retaining senior scientific and technical experts in a competitive market.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a scientific, technical or engineering discipline and 12 or more years of progressive experience in scientific, laboratory or technical services, including at least 5 years with commercial ownership of a service line, practice or portfolio and at least 5 years leading teams;

OR

  • Advanced degree (MSc, PhD or MBA) in a relevant discipline and 10 or more years of progressive experience with the same commercial and leadership content;

OR

  • An equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree (MSc or PhD) in a life science discipline, and an MBA or equivalent commercial qualification.
  • Experience in laboratory outsourcing, scientific managed services, CRO or CDMO environments, on either the provider or the customer side.
  • Experience operating across both North American and European markets.
  • Working knowledge of laboratory informatics (LIMS and ELN), laboratory automation and applied AI in laboratory operations.
  • A recognised external profile in scientific operations or laboratory services.

Working Environment:

  • The role may be based on the East Coast of the United States or in the United Kingdom, and requires working patterns that accommodate multiple time zones.
  • Travel of up to approximately 30 to 40 percent to customer sites, company locations, partner sites and industry events, including international travel.
  • Must be able to work in a laboratory or controlled environment requiring personal protective equipment (e.g. lab coat, safety glasses).
  • Job pace may be fast and job completion demands may be high.
  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position more than 25 percent of the time, and to move occasionally between labs, corridors, adjoining rooms and buildings on site.
  • Occasionally move or lift up to 25 pounds (potential for occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds).
  • Specific vision abilities required include, without limitation, close range and distance vision, colour vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Potential risk from lab-based hazards including but not limited to extreme temperature, biological materials and hazardous chemicals, and may be required to complete Medical Clearance, Respiratory Protection Training and Fit Testing.

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $190,000 to $230,000 + Bonus. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

PerkinElmer is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, or veteran status or any other characteristics protected by applicable law. PerkinElmer is committed to a culturally diverse workforce.

About Elavon

Knowledge / Skills / Experience required:

  • Broad commercial and financial acumen and awareness of issues involved in negotiating contracts and has ability to negotiate logically and constructively
  • Proven ability to develop and maintain an effective network of contacts and build relationships at all levels, internally and externally

jobs.title: Senior Accountant
jobs.excerpt: About WanderTravel is a $4 trillion industry running on software from the last century.
jobs.description:
About Wander

Travel is a $4 trillion industry running on software from the last century. We are fixing that. Wander.com is the leading marketplace for exceptional vacation homes with best-in-category guest satisfaction. WanderOS takes that same battle-tested engine and puts it in the hands of every property manager on Earth: conversion-optimized direct booking websites, automated guest marketing, and AI-powered distribution to millions of travelers. Operators own their brand, their bookings, and their guests. No middlemen.

Wander is led by a second-time founder and an all-star team from companies like Shopify. We are a Series B company gearing up for Series C, and product velocity has gone vertical: AI agents, payments, new distribution channels, and performance products, all shipping on a cadence most companies would call impossible. We call it Tuesday.

Our mission is to help people find their happy place. Our vision is to build the infrastructure for people to experience the world. If you want to make a dent in one of the largest industries on the planet, this is the place.

About the role

Wander runs two businesses on one engine: Wander.com, the leading marketplace for exceptional vacation homes, and WanderOS (wander.com/os), the operating system property managers use to run direct bookings, guest marketing, distribution, and payments. Money moves through both every day: guest bookings, host payouts, subscriptions, payment processing, and a growing stack of AI products. We need someone to sit inside Finance and own the accounting that keeps all of it accurate, closed on time, and ready for what comes next.

As our L6 Senior Accountant you will own the month-end close and the general ledger, and you will build the accounting foundation for a Series B company gearing up for Series C. This is an individual contributor position reporting to Wander's VP of Finance, working closely with our Accounting Supervisor, our external accounting and tax partners, and the Product and Engineering teams that build the systems the money flows through. You will not just be maintaining systems. You will be building them.

This role is remote across the US. If you are in Austin or San Francisco, we have offices waiting for you (SF is in the Presidio).

Level: L6 Senior Accountant

Years of experience set the level. This posting is for L6 Senior:

  • 5 to 8+ years of accounting experience, including time at a high-growth startup, a marketplace or SaaS company, or a public accounting firm serving them.
  • You own the close end to end and work with high autonomy in high ambiguity.
  • You are the go-to person on technical accounting questions for the finance team and the business.

What you'll do

Own the close and the general ledger

  • Own the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close: journal entries, accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, intercompany, and balance sheet reconciliations, accurately and on time, every time.
  • Prepare financial statements and variance analysis, and keep the books clean enough that any question can be answered in minutes.
  • Shorten the close every quarter. Document the process, automate the repeatable parts, and build the controls that let us scale.

Marketplace and SaaS revenue

  • Own revenue accounting across the business: guest bookings and host payouts on the marketplace, WanderOS subscriptions and usage, and payment processing, under ASC 606.
  • Reconcile payment processor and bank activity (Stripe and partners) to the ledger, and build the reconciliations that keep money movement tight as volume grows.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering so new products and pricing launch with the accounting already figured out, not retrofitted.

Operations: AP, AR, and payouts

  • Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, expense management, and payroll journal entries with our Accounting Supervisor.
  • Make sure hosts, vendors, and partners get paid correctly and on time, and that every dollar in and out is reconciled.

Audit, tax, and Series C readiness

  • Coordinate with external auditors on audit requests, workpapers, and filings, and prepare the company for its next audit cycle.
  • Support tax compliance with our external tax partners: income tax, sales and lodging taxes across jurisdictions, 1099s, and multi-state registrations.
  • Build the policies, controls, and documentation a Series C investor and a future public company auditor expect to see.

Immerse in the data and put AI to work

  • Own and evolve the finance systems stack: the general ledger, close tooling, expense and AP platforms, and integrations with product data.
  • Use AI tooling to automate routine reconciliations, flux analysis, and documentation so you can focus on the high-impact work only humans can do.

Communicate and influence

  • Translate the numbers for the VP of Finance, the founder, and the leadership team: what happened, why, and what it means.
  • Build high-trust relationships across Finance, Product, Engineering, Operations, and our external partners.

Who you are

  • 5 to 8+ years of accounting experience, with a significant track record owning a monthly close at a high-growth company. Startup, marketplace, or SaaS experience strongly preferred.
  • CPA (or equivalent) strongly preferred. Big 4 or public accounting experience is a plus.
  • Deep working knowledge of US GAAP, including ASC 606 revenue recognition. You can research a technical accounting question and write up a defensible position.
  • Hands-on with a modern general ledger (NetSuite, QuickBooks Online, or similar), close and reconciliation tooling, and payment processor data (Stripe or similar). Advanced spreadsheet skills; SQL is a plus.
  • Data-first analytical thinking: you reconcile to the penny and you can explain the variance.
  • Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain an accounting policy to an engineer and a founder in the same meeting.
  • High agency in high ambiguity: you figure it out, document it, and move on. You thrive on change rather than endure it, and you keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter).
  • Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling in a finance or operations context.
  • Hardcore. You care deeply about getting it right, you set a high bar, and you get it done.

Additional assets

  • Experience in travel, hospitality, vacation rentals, property management, or another marketplace with two-sided money movement.
  • Experience with sales and lodging tax compliance across US states, or with payments and money transmission accounting.
  • Experience preparing a company for its first audit, a financing, or a systems migration (for example QuickBooks to NetSuite).
  • Prior entrepreneurial experience: you ran a business, founded something, or were early at a startup.
  • A personal mantra of owning your own development. Tell us the courses, books, or mentors you used to level up your craft.

Compensation and benefits

  • Base salary: $100,000 to $110,000 USD. This is Series B startup market rate for the L6 Senior level, with placement in the range based on experience and location.
  • Meaningful equity. You will own a piece of what you build.
  • Health, dental, and vision coverage.
  • Remote-first across the US, with offices in Austin, TX and San Francisco (Presidio) if you want a desk.

Join us

You could spend the next few years closing the books at a company that changes twice a year. Or you could build the accounting foundation for the operating system of a $4 trillion industry, at a company that ships every week. Apply now.

Leadership

  • Build a high-performing global Tech Expansion organization.

jobs.excerpt: In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities.
jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description:

Position Summary

We are seeking a hands-on Document Control Supervisor to lead document control activities supporting construction, engineering, quality, procurement, subcontractors, suppliers, and project management functions.

This role will oversee document control processes, systems, governance, and personnel for construction programs and projects. The supervisor will ensure that controlled documents and project records are received, processed, reviewed, approved, distributed, retrieved, retained, and protected in accordance with project procedures, the project Quality Management System, contractual requirements, client standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.

The successful candidate will build order out of complexity, strengthen document control practices across field and office teams, and serve as a trusted partner to Project Managers, Construction Managers, Engineering, Quality, and Operations leaders. This position will also administer and improve systems such as Procore and SharePoint, provide training and user support, and drive continuous improvement throughout the project lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Document Control and Records Management

  • Lead project document control activities supporting construction, engineering, quality, procurement, project management, subcontractors, suppliers, and field operations.
  • Develop, maintain, and administer document control processes and procedures for identifying, receiving, processing, reviewing, approving, revising, distributing, filing, preserving, retrieving, and retaining controlled documents and records.
  • Administer controlled documents in accordance with the project Quality Management System, applicable ASME NQA-1 requirements, project procedures, client requirements, and contractual obligations.
  • Control engineering and project documents, including drawings, specifications, procedures, work packages, vendor documents, quality records, change requests, RFIs/RFPs, and construction documentation.
  • Ensure personnel have access to the current, approved revisions of drawings, specifications, procedures, work packages, and other controlled documents.
  • Maintain document registers, revision histories, document status information, distribution records, transmittals, and other required tracking tools.
  • Process new and revised documents through established review and approval workflows.
  • Identify and prevent the unintended use of obsolete, superseded, or unapproved documents.
  • Maintain document traceability and ensure controlled records are complete, legible, accurate, retrievable, secure, and protected from unauthorized access or alteration.
  • Ensure the collection and retention of construction documentation throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Manage the as-built documentation process and support the preparation, compilation, and turnover of final project records and closeout packages.
  • Coordinate the handover of documents and records to Operations during construction and project closeout.

Systems Administration and Governance

  • Administer, configure, and improve document management platforms, including Procore, SharePoint, and related electronic document management systems.
  • Establish and maintain project repositories, file structures, naming conventions, metadata, permissions, workflows, document numbering, revision control, and distribution requirements.
  • Provide oversight of employees, contractors, subcontractors, and other users operating within Procore and other project repositories.
  • Perform quality control reviews of metadata, document content, cross-references, required signatures, revision status, and associated records.
  • Manage user access, permissions, administrative controls, and periodic access audits.
  • Ensure document control systems and records management practices align with client standards, project requirements, governance policies, and applicable legal, contractual, regulatory, and quality obligations.
  • Safeguard confidential and protected information through appropriate storage, handling, distribution, access, and retention practices.
  • Work with IT and project stakeholders to troubleshoot system issues, resolve access or workflow problems, and support system enhancements.

Project and Stakeholder Support

  • Coordinate document control activities with Quality, Engineering, Construction, Procurement, Supply Chain, Contracts, project management, subcontractors, suppliers, and external client representatives.
  • Partner with Project Managers, Construction Managers, and Operations leaders to tailor document control solutions to project needs while maintaining consistent standards.
  • Monitor document workflows and resolve outstanding reviews, approvals, distribution issues, missing information, and other document control discrepancies.
  • Ensure Document Control Coordinators regularly engage with site teams to confirm compliance with client standards, document numbering requirements, turnover requirements, and project procedures.
  • Support audits, surveillances, assessments, inspections, and compliance reviews by retrieving controlled documents, records, and objective evidence.
  • Verify that document control activities and records meet applicable project, quality, contractual, and client requirements.
  • Identify process gaps and recommend practical improvements that enhance accuracy, efficiency, traceability, and user adoption.

Leadership, Training, and Continuous Improvement

  • Provide direction, work coordination, supervision, mentoring, and performance support to Document Control Coordinators and other assigned personnel.
  • Assign work, establish service expectations, monitor performance, and ensure timely and accurate document control support to active projects.
  • Develop and deliver training for Document Controllers, field personnel, project teams, and system users.
  • Prepare clear training materials, user guides, standard operating procedures, and onboarding resources that support quick and consistent adoption.
  • Coach project teams and reinforce disciplined document management practices through regular communication, touchpoints, and feedback.
  • Revise existing processes and procedures when project, client, system, or regulatory requirements change.
  • Capture lessons learned and implement continuous improvements across the document control function.
  • Stay current on emerging document management technologies, automation, and AI-enabled tools that may reduce manual effort and improve quality, accuracy, and accessibility.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Typically 10 years of related experience, including 3 in a supervisory or management role in document control, records management, project controls, quality records, project information management, or a related discipline.
  • Experience supporting industrial construction, engineering, infrastructure, transportation, energy, DOE, nuclear, federal, or other highly regulated projects.
  • Experience administering controlled technical documents and revision processes.
  • Experience with Procore; experience administering or supporting SharePoint is also required or strongly preferred.
  • Experience with electronic document management systems, document repositories, and document workflow processes.
  • Working knowledge of document numbering, revision control, distribution, transmittals, records retention, document status tracking, and access control.
  • Experience supporting engineering drawings, specifications, procedures, work packages, vendor documents, construction records, and/or quality records.
  • Experience with construction documentation such as change requests, RFIs, RFPs, submittals, work packages, and as-built records.
  • Experience developing and maintaining document control processes, procedures, standard operating procedures, training materials, user guides, or governance documentation.
  • Experience leading, supervising, or coordinating Document Control Coordinators, contractors, or other system users.
  • Familiarity with construction closeout documentation, project turnover, audit readiness, records retrieval, retention requirements, and compliance reporting.
  • Excellent computer skills, including advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, Outlook, and SharePoint.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Acrobat and/or Bluebeam.
  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, client service, and stakeholder communication skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, changing requirements, multiple stakeholders, and time-sensitive deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
  • High level of discretion, dependability, professionalism, accountability, and reliability when handling confidential or protected information.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Construction Management, Quality, Information Management, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent education and experience may be considered.
  • Experience working under an ASME NQA-1, DOE, USACE, or comparable quality program.
  • Previous EPC, nuclear, energy, industrial construction, infrastructure, or large-scale construction experience.
  • Experience supporting federal or highly regulated clients.
  • Experience with USACE RMS or similar client-mandated project management and reporting systems.
  • Membership or certification through ARMA, an Enterprise Content Management organization, or a related professional organization.
  • Experience administering SharePoint sites, libraries, workflows, metadata, permissions, and document templates.
  • Experience supporting project turnover and final records packages.
  • Familiarity with quality audits, surveillances, assessments, and objective evidence retrieval.
  • Experience using workflow automation, reporting tools, or AI-enabled solutions to improve document control performance.

Core Competencies

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Process Leadership: Ability to design, standardize, implement, and improve practical document control processes.
  • Quality and Compliance: Strong understanding of controlled documents, quality records, traceability, revision control, and retention requirements.
  • Systems Proficiency: Ability to administer and support Procore, SharePoint, and related document management systems.
  • Attention to Detail: Consistent focus on accuracy, completeness, metadata quality, signatures, cross-references, and document status.
  • Communication: Ability to make complex requirements clear and practical for field personnel, project teams, clients, and senior leaders.
  • Problem Solving: Sound business judgment and the ability to resolve complex issues with appropriate escalation and follow-through.
  • Leadership: Ability to lead, coach, train, and develop a small team while coordinating work across multiple project stakeholders.
  • Adaptability: Ability to respond effectively to changing projects, clients, systems, and regulatory requirements.
  • Accountability: Demonstrated dependability, punctuality, focus, ownership of assigned work, and ability to meet deadlines.
  • Teamwork: Professional attitude and ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.

Key Relationships

  • Reports To: Operations
  • Matrixed Alignment: Director, Quality
  • Supervises: Document Control Coordinators and assigned document control personnel
  • Internal Partners: Project Managers, Construction Managers, Engineering, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, Contracts, IT, Operations, and field teams
  • External Partners: Clients, subcontractors, suppliers, vendors, and external auditors or assessors

Success Measures

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

  • Consistent use of approved document control processes across assigned projects.
  • Timely processing, review, approval, distribution, and retrieval of project documents.
  • Accurate document registers, metadata, revision histories, transmittals, and status records.
  • Effective prevention of obsolete or superseded document use.
  • Strong Procore, SharePoint, and repository governance.
  • Audit-ready project records and successful closeout and turnover packages.
  • Effective training, adoption, and support for field and project teams.
  • Timely resolution of workflow, access, quality, and compliance issues.
  • Improved efficiency, traceability, and user experience across the document control function.

Other Duties

This job description is not intended to include every duty, responsibility, or activity required for the role. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time, with or without notice.

Our intelligent employees drive the state of the art as they provide services and solutions in the areas of defense, security, intelligence, infrastructure, and environmental. We promote a culture of excellence and close-knit teams that take pride in delivering, protecting, and sustaining our nation's most critical assets, from Earth to cyberspace. Throughout the company, our people are anticipating what’s next to deliver the solutions our customers need now.Salary Range: $88,400.00 - $154,700.00We value our employees and want our employees to take care of their overall wellbeing, which is why we offer best-in-class benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), 401(k), life insurance, flexible work schedules, and holidays to fit your busy lifestyle!This position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will continue to be posted for an average of 30 days until a qualified applicant is selected or the position has been cancelled.Parsons is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other protected status.We truly invest and care about our employee’s wellbeing and provide endless growth opportunities as the sky is the limit, so aim for the stars! In some cases, the Senior Commercial Title Examiner role requires gathering information and creating or revising a commitment of title before passing along to a Commercial Title Officer or Underwriter.

•Experience working directly with Underwriters and Attorneys

Review title commitments for accuracy and make necessary revisions

May provide underwriting interpretation within established guidelines

Other duties as assigned

7 + years Commercial title examination experience, previous MI experience required

Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize and provide timely follow up

Excellent verbal and written communication with internal and external customers

Natural curiosity, enjoys researching the history and background of transactions, analyzing, and evaluating records

High School diploma or equivalent

The Technical Account Manager owns the post-sale technical relationship for an assigned book of customer accounts — driving product adoption, environment health, and long-term value realization in close partnership with the wider Customer Success team.

Onboarding & implementation

Staffing Sales Strategy & Revenue Growth

Website & Content Management

CMS Administration

  • Plan and organize demos and product testing sessions with stakeholders to gather feedback

Quality Assurance & Optimization

  • Experience managing project timelines, risk mitigation and dependency management
  • Skilled in facilitating communication between technical teams and non-technical stakeholders to ensure alignment on execution, scope constraints, and delivery expectations
  • Proficiency in facilitating and driving consistency across all Agile ceremonies (program increments, portfolio planning, goals setting, sprint planning, reviews, retrospectives, and daily scrums)

Highlights

  • Location: Poland, Remote (core hours 9:00–18:00 CET)
  • Languages: Fluent in English and Russian
  • Reports to VP, Product

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building alarge and complex product ecosystemthat serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a moderncheckout experience and customizable widgets(each a standalone SPA),donor, organization, and partner portals,admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

The Lab

Fundraise Up is investing in a Lab function to explore new product lines and step-change growth opportunities. The Lab operates like a small startup: rapidly turning ambiguous opportunities into shipped pilots and clear investment decisions.

About The Role

This is a senior individual contributor PM role for someone who thrives in ambiguity and can personally drive discovery, experimentation, and early delivery with engineering and design.
The core mandate is to build and validate high-uncertainty bets and make explicit Scale / Iterate / Pivot / Kill calls based on evidence.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain a prioritized Lab portfolio/backlog with clear hypotheses, expected upside, effort, dependencies, and status.
  • Define the riskiest assumptions for each bet and design experiments with explicit kill criteria.
  • Run fast experiments (spikes, prototypes, wizard-of-oz, pilots) and ship “just enough” product to learn—without overbuilding.
  • Partner tightly with engineering and design to deliver pilots and instrument them to capture meaningful signals.
  • Synthesize outcomes into crisp decisions: Scale / Iterate / Pivot / Kill—and prevent “zombie projects.”
  • Create lightweight decision logs and learning summaries to keep leadership and GTM aligned.
  • Identify GTM dependencies early (positioning, enablement, pricing, legal, support, etc.) and coordinate cross-functionally.
  • When signal is strong, prepare a clean handoff package (what was validated, evidence, remaining risks, success metrics, recommended scaling plan).

What Great Looks Like in 9 Months

  • A single, visible Lab portfolio exists with clear statuses, owners/counterparts, and next decision points.
  • A repeatable prioritization method is in place (signals, confidence, upside, GTM dependency, effort).
  • A 4–8 week experiment plan is defined and executed.
  • Multiple experiments are completed and end with explicit decisions (no zombie initiatives).
  • Engineering/design counterparts are named per top initiative and working cadence is established.

How the Lab team works

  • One permanent owner at the start: you.
  • Engineering and design support are assigned on demand per initiative, and must be made explicit for each top-priority bet.
  • The biggest challenge is typically coordination with GTM, so crisp communication and early dependency management are critical.

Requirements

  • Senior PM experience in 0→1 / incubation / new bets (or equivalent track record).
  • Strong product judgment and technical fluency: can write specs, reason about feasibility, tradeoffs, instrumentation, and data needs.
  • Comfort operating as the driver: minimal delegation, maximal ownership.
  • Proven ability to run fast, scrappy experiments and move from ambiguity to decisions.
  • Strong communication: can produce concise decision logs, learning summaries, and alignment artifacts.
  • Uses AI as leverage for research, synthesis, prototyping, and analysis—while maintaining high-quality judgment.

Nice to have

  • Experience launching early-stage products into market with measurable adoption/revenue signals.
  • Experience working closely with GTM teams on positioning, enablement, and early go-to-market motion.

This Role Is Not For You If…

  • Stable roadmaps, long planning cycles, and incremental optimization.
  • Heavy reliance on others to structure specs, experiments, or execution.
  • Low tolerance for ambiguity or rapid direction changes.

Interview focus areas (signals we’ll assess)

  • Ability to turn ambiguous problems into sharp hypotheses and experiment plans.
  • Speed-to-learning and rigor in kill criteria.
  • Hands-on execution with engineering/design and ability to keep scope tight.
  • Quality of decision-making and clarity of written artifacts.
  • Cross-functional alignment (especially with GTM).

Why Work With Us

  • Real ownership over high-impact bets with the authority and team to pursue them
  • Leadership that values clear thinking over activity
  • Permission — and expectation — to kill bad ideas early
  • Access to real customers, real data, and real constraints
  • Flat structure, transparent culture, and equity participation

Compensation

  • The compensation range for this role is €5,800 - €6,700 gross.
  • Final compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, alignment with the role’s requirements and location.

Benefits

Our compensation package includes comprehensive benefits and perks, meaningful equity, and a competitive salary:

  • 31 days of paid time off
  • 100% paid telemedicine plan
  • Home office setup assistance
  • English learning courses
  • Professional education budget
  • Gym or swimming pool membership
  • Co-working support
  • Fully remote work

About EnerVenue, Inc.

EnerVenue is a Silicon Valley-based energy infrastructure company commercializing metal-hydrogen battery technology originally developed by NASA for the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. Founded in 2020 by Stanford Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue adapts this proven aerospace chemistry for grid-scale terrestrial energy storage, delivering batteries with 30,000+ cycle lifetimes, inherent fire-safety, and a 30-year design life.

In 2026, EnerVenue closed a $300 million Series B extension and is well capitalized for growth. Funds are being deployed to build a high-volume manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, targeting 250 MWh capacity by Q3 2026 and 1 GWh by 2027. EnerVenue has been named one of Time magazine's Top 10 US Green Technology Companies of 2025.

The Role
We are seeking a technically rigorous and customer-focused Energy Storage Applications Engineer to bridge the gap between our advanced energy storage technology and real-world deployment. This is a strategic, hands-on role critical to our mission. You will translate customer requirements into optimized system designs, validate performance across diverse use cases, and ensure our solutions deliver measurable value in the field. Acting as the technical backbone of the commercial process, you will support sales, marketing, product, and engineering teams with modeling, integration guidance, technical sales support, and application expertise.

Key Responsibilities
Lead the Technical Pre-Sales Process:

  • Serve as the primary technical partner to Sales throughout the commercial lifecycle—from initial qualification through contract execution.
  • Shape deal strategy by translating customer use cases, financial objectives, and operating constraints into technically optimized, commercially compelling storage solutions.

Translate Market Opportunities Into Bankable Proposals

  • Lead technical discovery sessions to define duty cycles, performance guarantees, augmentation strategies, and integration requirements.
  • Develop robust energy storage models that quantify lifetime performance, degradation, efficiency, availability, and ROI.
  • Produce detailed technical proposals and bid packages, including system sizing, single-line diagrams, performance assumptions, and compliance documentation.

Strengthen Technical Sales Enablement

  • Partner with Sales to respond to RFPs, RFIs, and technical due diligence requests with speed, accuracy, and credibility.
  • Support customer meetings, executive presentations, and contract negotiations as the technical authority.
  • Develop standardized tools, calculators, and modeling frameworks that improve proposal consistency, cycle time, and win rates.
  • Manage customer facing technical documentation and work alongside technical teams to generate documentation as necessary for project proposals.
  • Develop and/or review System designs, Single Lines, Layouts, Containerization, Performance guarantees, Availability guarantees, etc.

Amplify Marketing & Market Positioning

  • Collaborate with Marketing to develop application notes, white papers, case studies, and technical content that articulate differentiated value.
  • Translate complex engineering advantages into clear, benefit-driven messaging for target segments (utility-scale, C&I, microgrid).
  • Provide technical input for product launches, webinars, conference presentations, and thought leadership initiatives.

Accelerate Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Serve as a bridge from the Commercial team to Product and Engineering, ensuring customer requirements and emerging use cases inform the roadmap.
  • Support commissioning readiness and early deployment to protect performance assumptions made during the sales process.

Position Requirements
The ideal candidate likely spent the first part of his or her career building deep technical foundations in power systems, battery engineering, PV + storage integration, or grid-connected infrastructure—either at a leading OEM, EPC, developer, utility, or technology-driven energy company—where he or she developed rigorous analytical skills and a strong safety mindset. He or she has since operated in a fast-paced, customer-facing or scaling environment, applying that technical depth to commercial pursuits and supporting projects from early-stage feasibility through commissioning and field optimization.

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), including system design, applications engineering, integration, technical sales support, and service.
  • Demonstrated expertise designing multi-MW scale energy storage systems, with strong command of both DC and AC electrical design principles.
  • High level of technical aptitude spanning from battery cell fundamentals through C&I and utility-scale battery systems.
  • Strong working knowledge of secondary battery chemistries, degradation mechanisms, system architectures, and operational limitations across diverse duty cycles.
  • Practical experience with balance-of-system (BOS) equipment, including inverters, medium-voltage transformers, combiner boxes, DC/DC converters, EMS, and BMS platforms.
  • Strong knowledge of NEC and applicable regulatory codes and standards for PV and energy storage installations, including NFPA 70 (NEC), IEEE 1547, UL 9540, UL 1741, and other relevant global standards.
  • Solid understanding of how energy storage and PV projects are constructed, commissioned, and brought online.
  • Ability to interpret operational data, apply statistical analysis techniques, and produce clear, actionable reports.
  • Working knowledge of commercial contracts, performance guarantees, and how technical design and proposal assumptions must support contractual obligations.
  • Familiarity with competitive energy storage products in the market and the ability to clearly articulate differentiated technical value.
  • Proven ability to operate cross-functionally across engineering, product, sales, marketing, and field teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to meet tight deadlines, manage multiple priorities, and maintain accountability for deliverables.
  • Willingness and ability to travel 10–20% to support customer engagement, project development, site validation, and industry events.

Mandatory Core Competencies
Technical Depth & Range
You are equally comfortable discussing electrochemical behavior at the cell level and reviewing single-line diagrams for multi-MW grid-connected systems. You can move seamlessly between modeling software and a job site.

Pre-Sales & Commercial Orientation
You understand that technical precision underpins revenue. Your expertise turns technical jargon into marketing differentiation. You support proposals that stand up to RFP scrutiny, independent engineer review, and contractual performance guarantees.

Professional & Accountable
You meet commitments, communicate proactively, and maintain composure and clarity under tight timelines and high-stakes customer interactions.

Ideal Mindset & Competencies
Bridge Builder (Between Engineering And Revenue)
They see themselves as a strategic enabler of growth. Their technical clarity accelerates deal cycles, increases win rates, and strengthens customer confidence.

Application-First Thinker
They design around real operating profiles—capacity firming, arbitrage, peak shaving, resilience, grid services—ensuring systems are optimized for performance and economics. They are also a code master, ensuring all stakeholders are aligned with NEC, IEEE, UL, and applicable global standards.

Commercially Fluent Engineer
They understand contracts, guarantees, liquidated damages risk, and bankability requirements—and ensure technical proposals align with those realities.

Market-Aware Technologist
They track competitor capabilities and industry standards closely, positioning EnerVenue’s technology with precision and credibility.

Disciplined Under Pressure
They thrive under deadlines, balancing technical thoroughness with commercial urgency, and consistently deliver high-quality work on schedule.

Forward-Thinking & Creative
They anticipate evolving grid needs, emerging use cases, and new commercial models—bringing fresh thinking to how energy storage is designed, positioned, and deployed.

What EnerVenue Offers

  • Unique opportunity to own full end-to-end technical application engineering work of a disruptive long-duration metal-hydrogen energy storage technology in the US, the company’s key APAC strategic market
  • Direct alignment with EnerVenue’s global headquarters in Silicon Valley and joint technical roadmap planning with Stanford University R&D team
  • Competitive compensation package for mid-level technical leadership role including base salary and project performance bonus tied to successful bid delivery and project win rate
  • Mid-level technical management position backed by top-tier global investors, with clear gigawatt-scale production capacity expansion roadmap based out of Changzhou, China to fully support US market supply
  • Join a mission-driven team developing 30-year service-life grid infrastructure energy storage equipment, rather than short-cycle consumer & EV lithium-ion batteries
  • Full technical training resources, access to global electrochemical R&D data and field test cases, plus funding for US industry conferences and standard certification upgrades

Every day, thousands of business travelers across the world use our software built on modern technology.

jobs.description:
FirstEnergy at a Glance 

 

We are a forward-thinking electric utility powered by a diverse team of employees committed to making customers’ lives brighter, the environment better and our communities stronger.  

 

FirstEnergy (NYSE: FE) is dedicated to integrity, safety, reliability and operational excellence. Headquartered in Akron, Ohio, FirstEnergy includes one of the nation's largest investor-owned electric systems, more than 24,000 miles of transmission lines that connect the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, and a regulated generating fleet with a total capacity of more than 3,500 megawatts.  

 

About the Opportunity  

 

This is an open position with FirstEnergy Service Co., a subsidiary of FirstEnergy Corp. [FEU].

We are seeking a highly motivated and talented individual to join our Project Management Project Controls team as a Project Scheduler in the Construction and Design Services organization. We welcome candidates with varying levels of experience. The outlined responsibilities will apply to all positions. The level at which you join the organization will be determined based on your qualifications and prior experience.

FirstEnergy takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. In addition, your actual base salary will depend on various factors such as your skills, qualifications, and experience.

The estimated pay range for this role is $74,375- $112,200. The pay range for certain locations, including the state of New Jersey, include a 20% differential to account for an increased cost of living, making the pay range $89,250 - $134,640.

Responsibilities include:

  • As a mid-level scheduler, you would be expected to have more experience and expertise in project scheduling using Primavera P6. You should be comfortable working independently and capable of handling more complex projects. Your responsibilities would involve a higher level of independence in managing schedules and collaborating with project teams. You may even be tasked with assisting less experienced schedulers and team members by providing guidance, training, and support.
  • As a senior-level scheduler, you would be considered an expert in project scheduling, with extensive experience in managing complex projects and mentoring less experienced schedulers. You would play a critical role in guiding project teams, identifying and/or participating in process improvement initiatives, and ensuring successful project delivery.

Specific job responsibilities for every level may vary depending on the organization's needs and the complexity of the projects you become involved in, but here are some common tasks you might be expected to perform:

  1. Data Entry and Maintenance: Inputting project data into the Primavera P6 system, including project activities, durations, resources, and relationships between tasks. You will also be responsible for regularly updating and maintaining the schedule as the project progresses.
  2. Schedule Monitoring: Assisting in monitoring project progress by comparing actual work completed to the planned schedule. Identifying discrepancies and helping to develop corrective action plans.
  3. Generating Reports: Supporting and producing regular schedule reports and schedule updates for project managers. This may involve extracting data from P6 and presenting it in a clear and concise manner.
  4. Resource Management: Assisting in managing project resources by ensuring they are properly assigned to activities, and responsible groups are identified accurately.
  5. Risk Assessment: Supporting the identification and analysis of potential schedule risks and assisting in developing mitigation strategies.
  6. Collaboration: Working with the project team to collect information, verify progress, and ensure that the schedule reflects the most up-to-date status of the project.
  7. Training and Learning: Continuously learning and improving your knowledge of Primavera P6, project scheduling best practices, and project management processes and practices.
  8. Adherence to Standards: Following established scheduling procedures, company guidelines, and industry best practices to maintain data integrity and consistency.

Qualifications include:

  • Bachelor's degree in project management, engineering, construction management, business administration or related degree with a minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience or, in lieu of a degree, a minimum of 4 years of relevant work experience. Relevant work may include project scheduling, planning, or project management.
  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in project scheduling, planning, or project management. Relevant experience includes hands-on experience in developing, maintaining, and analyzing project schedules using tools like Primavera P6, ideally within construction or engineering environments, with demonstrated ability to work independently and collaborate across project teams.
  • Professional certifications related to project management and scheduling is a plus.
  • Proficiency in project scheduling software such as Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or other industry-standard tools is a plus.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to effectively convey information.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities concurrently.
  • Familiarity with construction and design services industry practices and terminology is a plus.
  • Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

Benefits, Compensation & Workforce Diversity   

 

At FirstEnergy, employees are key to our success. We depend on their talents to meet the challenges of our changing business environment. We are committed to rewarding individual and team efforts through our total rewards philosophy which includes competitive pay plus incentive compensation, a company-sponsored pension plan, 401(k) savings plan with matching employer contribution, a choice of medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, and life insurance programs, as well as skills development training with tuition reimbursement. Please visit our website at www.firstenergycorp.com to learn more about all of our employee rewards programs. FirstEnergy proudly supports workforce diversity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, or status as a qualified individual with a disability. No recruiters or agencies without a previously signed contract. Unable to sponsor or transfer H-1B visas at this time.   

 

Safety   

 

Safety is a core value for FirstEnergy and is essential to all of our business activities. We ensure employees have the tools, information, and processes to perform their duties in a manner that assures safety for themselves, their co-workers, our customers and the public. Our goals are to provide a safe work environment, to maintain an accident-free, injury-free workplace, and to promote and maintain public safety. To meet these goals, we dedicate ourselves to achieving world-class safety standards.
