Our client is a global technology organization that develops digital products and services used by businesses and consumers across multiple markets.

The organization operates in a highly data-driven environment where marketing, sales, product, analytics, creative, and technology teams collaborate to accelerate customer acquisition, engagement, and revenue growth.

For this opportunity, the marketing team is focused on developing sophisticated multi-channel programs that move priority Mid-Market audiences and accounts through the buying journey and generate measurable pipeline.

About the Role

We are looking for a Staff Performance Marketing Manager to own multi-channel demand generation programs that drive pipeline for the Mid-Market business.

This is a senior individual contributor role responsible for building and running programs that move priority audiences and accounts through the funnel toward SQLs, SQOs, and pipeline.

You will own a portfolio of always-on and campaign-connected programs end to end, including strategy, build, execution, testing, measurement, and optimization. Programs may include account-based initiatives, lifecycle marketing, owned-channel nurture, and signal-based plays.

Lifecycle marketing is a core channel within this portfolio, but this is not a lifecycle-only role. Success requires understanding where audiences and accounts are stalled and building targeted, multi-channel programs that accelerate progression and generate measurable business outcomes.

Why This Opportunity?

This role offers significant ownership over programs directly connected to demand generation and pipeline growth.

You'll work at the intersection of performance marketing, demand generation, lifecycle, ABM/ABX, marketing automation, analytics, and creative, partnering with multiple teams to design and execute sophisticated marketing programs.

As a Staff-level contributor, you'll also serve as a senior resource for campaign and lifecycle marketers, helping strengthen progression logic, testing discipline, and marketing automation expertise.

What You'll Do

Demand Generation & Account Growth

  • Diagnose where priority accounts and audiences are stalled across the buying journey and build targeted programs to improve progression.
  • Design programs that move audiences toward SQLs, SQOs, and pipeline.
  • Own a portfolio of planned and emerging account-growth plays.
  • Test, optimize, scale, modify, or stop programs based on performance evidence.
  • Launch signal-based programs when new opportunities emerge, including mid-quarter.

Lifecycle & Multi-Channel Marketing

  • Plan and manage end-to-end lifecycle campaigns, including onboarding, nurture, retention, and win-back.
  • Own program strategy, creative development, execution, measurement, and optimization.
  • Partner with campaign leads on audience progression strategies for major campaigns.
  • Design, build, launch, and optimize the programs required to activate those strategies.
  • Balance lifecycle initiatives with broader demand generation and account-growth programs.

Marketing Automation, Testing & Analytics

  • Set up, test, QA, and deploy programs using Marketo, Eloqua, Braze, HubSpot, or equivalent marketing automation platforms.

Independent certification bodies verify compliance with the 4C requirements. 4C was developed in a comprehensive and transparent multi-stakeholder process involving coffee/cocoa producers, trade and industry, as well as organizations from civil society around the world. 4C aims to move the entire coffee or cocoa sector towards sustainability practices. 4C operates in 25 countries and is one of the largest certification systems in the coffee sector.

Since 2020, the 4C System has evolved into a robust, benchmarked standard, defining clear social, environmental, and economic criteria. Alongside certification, we provide innovative solutions to help companies comply with global regulations and strengthen responsible supply chains in a changing world.

4C Services GmbH, the operator of 4C certification system, is seeking to recruit a highly motivated freelance auditor to conduct integrity assessments within the framework of the 4C Integrity Program.

  • Planning, preparing, and conducting 4C integrity assessments at certified 4C Units, Intermediary and Final Buyers of 4C certified coffee and Certification Bodies cooperation with 4C, with focus on:
    • Traceability
    • Social issues such as child labour, forced labour, fair and safe working conditions
    • Environmental issues such as deforestation, biodiversity and soil conservation, and pesticide use
  • General support to 4C System users in countries of East and West Africa, Asia, or Latin America regarding communication, meetings, translation of documents, etc.
  • Contribution to the continuous development of the 4C System and the 4C Integrity Program

About the job

Cosmic AC is Tether Data's GPU compute and managed inference platform: GPU containers, managed inference endpoints and platform observability, delivered as a self-hosted package on Kubernetes, with a control plane written in JavaScript. The platform is expanding from orchestrating workloads on a managed cluster to owning the full stack on bare-metal GPU infrastructure: a managed Slurm scheduling layer for internal research and model-training teams first, and our own Kubernetes control plane for inference tenancy after that.

The Technical Lead owns the architecture and delivery of that stack and leads the engineering team building it: about twelve engineers across backend, frontend, DevOps, QA and documentation, distributed across Europe and India. The role reports to the Senior Technical Product Manager for Cosmic AC, who owns scope, sequencing and partner commitments; the Technical Lead owns architecture, implementation and delivery plans, line-manages the engineers, and is the primary technical interface to our infrastructure partners.

This is a hands-on infrastructure leadership role with a fixed delivery window in its first six months. It is not a research role, not a pure Kubernetes SRE role, and not a management-only role.

Responsibilities

Architecture. Own the platform architecture end to end: architecture proposals, high-level and low-level designs, driven through review and kept current as the baseline.

Team leadership. Lead and line-manage a distributed team across backend (Node.js), frontend (React), DevOps, QA and documentation: engineering standards, code and design review, release gates, one-to-ones, growth and performance input.

Bare-metal GPU scheduling layer. Design, build and operate a managed Slurm service for research users: controller and accounting, partitions and login nodes, node onboarding and acceptance, driver and CUDA baseline and upgrades, stalled-job and node-health detection, drain and autohealing, storage visibility, identity and isolation.

Kubernetes control plane and GPU enablement. Own cluster bootstrap and lifecycle on partner-provided bare metal, NVIDIA GPU Operator and Network Operator, VM-based GPU isolation (KubeVirt and VFIO), and day-2 operations: upgrades, backup and recovery, node replacement.

Managed inference at scale. Serving architecture, multi-GPU and multi-node parallelism, autoscaling, request routing and endpoint reliability; confidential-compute-capable capacity for sensitive workloads.

Observability and operations. Metrics, logging, alerting and SLOs across control plane, GPU fleet and application tiers; incident response and post-incident review; an on-call model a small team can sustain.

Partners and vendors. Primary technical interface to infrastructure partners and vendors: turning requirements into written specifications and acceptance tests, running escalations to closure, and providing technical input to capacity planning and hardware sourcing.

Internal consumers. Work directly with research, model-training and product teams to translate their workloads into platform requirements, and broker capacity when it is short.

Hiring. Complete the platform team and set the technical bar for the engineers who join it.

Requirements

Must have

  • Experience. Eight or more years of hands-on engineering, including at least three leading teams that build and operate infrastructure platforms other teams depend on. Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science or engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Slurm at scale, hands on. Has run slurmctld and slurmdbd for real users: partitions, QoS and priority, accounting, prolog and epilog, node health scripting, upgrades with jobs on the system. Ideally has operated an HPC or GPU training cluster for a research population.

  • GPU fleet operation on bare metal. NVIDIA driver and CUDA lifecycle, Fabric Manager and NVSwitch behaviour on SXM systems, DCGM-based health and utilisation, MIG, node burn-in and acceptance.

  • High-performance interconnects. InfiniBand fabric and subnet configuration, RDMA, SR-IOV, and diagnosing multi-node NCCL performance problems.

  • Linux systems depth. Kernel modules and drivers, PCIe passthrough and vfio-pci, cgroups and namespaces, performance tuning for compute-heavy workloads.

  • Production Kubernetes operation, not just deployment: control plane, upgrades, CNI and CSI, operators and custom controllers, multi-tenancy design.

  • HPC storage and data movement. Shared filesystems (VAST, Lustre, NFS), node-local NVMe caching, distributing large model weights and datasets across many nodes.

  • Observability and operations. Prometheus, Grafana and Loki or equivalents, SLOs, incident response and post-incident review.

  • Working fluency in JavaScript and sufficient to review a control plane, CLI and worker services with authority and to make architecture decisions on them. Not a feature-development requirement.

  • A shipped platform with real users. A multi-tenant IaaS or PaaS, or a research computing service: resource isolation, quotas, usage metering, and user-facing API and CLI surfaces.

  • Leadership that stays in the code. People management across time zones, cross-track review, written architecture decisions with alternatives recorded, and the ability to tell a partner or an executive no with reasons.

  • Excellent written and spoken English. Most partner and leadership work happens in writing.

  • Location. Fully remote, based between UTC and UTC+5:30 so the working day overlaps both Europe and India, where the team and its partners work. Occasional travel to partner sites and team events.

Desirable

  • Slurm operators on Kubernetes (Soperator, Slinky) or Kubernetes-native schedulers (Kueue, Volcano, KAI, Kubeflow Trainer).

  • Modern serving stacks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM): parallelism strategies, quantisation trade-offs, GPU memory planning.

  • VM and container isolation for multi-tenant GPU compute (KubeVirt, Kata Containers, QEMU and KVM, Firecracker); confidential computing (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, NVIDIA confidential-compute mode).

  • Cluster API and kubeadm, Cilium, NVSentinel-class autohealing, infrastructure as code and GitOps.

  • Time on the operator side of a GPU cloud, a national or university HPC centre, or an AI lab's platform team.

  • Peer-to-peer or distributed-systems background.

About the Role

We're looking for a Principal Server Engineer to own the backend systems powering our live games - services currently supporting 1M+ DAU. You'll be responsible for performance, scalability, and reliability at the core of our infrastructure, working closely with the engineering team on everything from schema design to incident response.

Experience: 8+ years

Nice to Have

  • CI/CD and DevOps experience (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) plus monitoring/alerting (Prometheus, Datadog)
  • Strong grasp of networking protocols — WebSockets, gRPC/HTTP2, UDP/TCP tuning for low-latency real-time systems

Requirements

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain Go/Python backend services for live, high-traffic game titles
  • Own database schema design and query performance across PostgreSQL systems
  • Drive horizontal scaling strategy - optimizing CPU/memory footprint and reducing lock contention over vertical scaling
  • Profile and resolve memory leaks, CPU spikes, and deadlocks in production
  • Lead root-cause investigations for performance issues and outages, from detection through resolution
  • Architect and maintain in-memory caching/state layers (Redis/KeyDB/Memcached)
  • Design and run load tests to surface breaking points ahead of release

Requirements

Crucial

  • Deep Go & Python expertise — language internals, execution models, and performance tuning (goroutine management, GC tuning, zero-allocation techniques)
  • Strong PostgreSQL fluency — scalable schema design, query plan analysis, index strategy optimization, with real examples of resolving bottlenecks via data layout or query architecture changes
  • Proven experience scaling systems supporting 350k+ DAU, with a horizontal-scaling-first philosophy (efficient serialization/deserialization via Protobuf/MsgPack, reduced lock contention)
  • Hands-on profiling experience — identifying and resolving memory leaks, CPU spikes, and deadlocks
  • At least 2 concrete examples of complex production performance issues or outages, including root cause analysis and resolution methodology
  • At least 2 released production projects as a core backend engineer handling live traffic

Important

  • Hands-on experience with Redis, KeyDB, or Memcached — caching, rate-limiting, state management, including cache stampede mitigation, serialization overhead, and eviction policy design
  • Solid TDD/BDD judgment and practical load-testing experience (e.g., Artillery)
  • Practical experience with the Nakama framework — custom Go/Lua modules, matchmakers, storage engine, real-time multiplayer sockets
  • Practical GCP/Google App Engine experience — deploying, monitoring, and scaling serverless/container services

Benefits

  • Market competitive, tax-free USD salaries
  • Paid Time Off
  • Annual Performance Reviews

About Wingz, Inc.

Wingz is a rideshare platform focused on Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT). Our network of compassionate, credentialed drivers helps vulnerable populations gain access to the care they need.

About the role

  • Market Operations keeps our markets running: enough verified drivers on the road, every trip assigned before the day begins, and every trip completed on time. You'll own a piece of that and be measured on it. This is a decision-making role, not a scripted one — you'll make calls, act, and explain your reasoning afterward.

What you'll do

If assigned to Driver Onboarding & Activation

  • Make fast first contact with new driver applicants and guide them through the application
  • Run onboarding interviews, group and 1:1, and decide who advances
  • Review driver documents for accuracy and compliance, and coach applicants through corrections
  • Coordinate background checks and screenings, and follow up until cleared
  • Run activation calls so new drivers are confident on the app before their first trip
  • Keep the roster current: expiration outreach, reactivation checks, and removing inactive drivers

If assigned to Dispatch & Scheduling

  • Build driver schedules and assign trips against them
  • Sweep the current week for schedule gaps and fill them before trips go uncovered
  • Work inside our AI-assisted dispatching tools, producing and acting on the daily output
  • Flag where the tooling gets it wrong so it improves
  • Notify drivers of schedule changes

If assigned to OTP Specialist

  • Monitor on-time performance live and intervene before a trip goes late, not after
  • Own urgent trip reassignments end to end: the decision, driver contact, and resolution
  • Keep clients informed before they have to ask
  • Step in when leads are tied up so nothing waits in a queue

If assigned to Routing Specialist

  • Build and adjust routes for efficiency and reliability
  • Make sure drivers activate GPS well ahead of pickup
  • Chase and coach drivers who don't, before it becomes a data gap
  • Protect billing and claims accuracy by keeping trip data complete

If assigned to Market Associate

  • Cover a portion of all three areas above in a newer or smaller market
  • Shift week to week toward whatever is currently limiting the market
  • Flag early which area is about to break

Every Market Operations Associate, in every area

  • Own your daily and weekly targets, and know where you stand without being asked
  • Resolve problems in your area rather than handing them off
  • Escalate what's genuinely above your authority, with what you've already tried and what you recommend
  • Keep driver and trip records accurate in every system you touch
  • Improve the procedures you work from, and document the ones that don't exist yet
  • Cross-train as backup on one adjacent area
  • Bring us patterns, not just incidents

What you'll need

  • 2-4 years in operations, dispatch, logistics, or program coordination, a role where you owned an outcome, not just a queue
  • Sound judgment without a script. Much of this work has no procedure for the situation in front of you
  • Comfort with tradeoffs. Some days you can cover one trip or the other, not both, and you'll need to decide quickly and defend the call
  • Comfort being measured daily. You should want the scoreboard, not avoid it
  • Ability to hold several threads at once and switch between them without dropping any
  • Strong written and verbal communication — most areas involve daily calls with drivers
  • Composure when things break. Some days are interrupt-driven and won't go as planned
  • Detail accuracy where a missed date or wrong record has real consequences
  • Strong spreadsheet skills and the ability to learn new tools quickly
  • Willingness to work ET hours, including weekend or holiday rotation depending on assignment
  • Reliable high-speed internet and a quiet space for video calls

Bonus Points

  • NEMT, healthcare transportation, or other regulated service experience
  • Dispatch, fleet, or last-mile operations background
  • Applicant tracking or recruiting platform experience
  • Experience running group interviews or high-volume onboarding
  • Experience with AI-assisted operational tooling

Why Wingz?

  • Mission-driven work that makes a tangible difference in people’s lives.
  • 100% remote work culture
  • A small, agile team where your impact is felt every day.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits.

jobs.description:
This role is part of our Usersnap team, one of our growing brands at saas.group.

Profile Overview

Usersnap is building AI-driven capabilities into the core of the product, from automated setup to intelligent surveys, contextual analysis, and reporting that generates itself based on connectors. We're looking for a hands-on AI Lead / Engineering Manager to lead the small engineering team that ships these capabilities, and to set the technical direction while doing it.

This is a player-coach role. You'll write and review code, make architecture calls, and define what "good" looks like for AI-native development. You'll also own team coordination, delivery timelines, workload allocation, and follow-through, so that work planned is work shipped, reliably and at production quality.

This is a full-time, engineering-led role. It is not combined with product management: the technical leadership scope is substantial on its own, and you'll partner with Product rather than absorb it.

AI capability is becoming core to Usersnap's product and go-to-market, especially as we move upmarket. You'll be the person who makes sure it ships well.

Your immediate impact in the first 3-6 months will be:

  • You'll have established a clear delivery rhythm for the team: shared priorities, realistic timelines, visible workload, and projects that get followed through to launch
  • You'll have assessed the current state of the codebase, tooling, and practices, and set out a concrete engineering bar covering observability, testing, security, and architecture
  • You'll have shipped at least one AI-powered feature to production with the team, from prototype through launch, using timeboxed AI development
  • You'll have built a strong working relationship with Product and the rest of the company, and be seen as a reliable owner of ambiguous, technically complex work
  • You'll have raised the team's standards while keeping people motivated and engaged

Your responsibilities

Team leadership and delivery

  • Own team coordination, delivery timelines, workload allocation, and project follow-through for a small engineering team
  • Keep work moving: break down ambiguous goals, sequence them with Product, flag slippage early, and make sure commitments are met
  • Give clear, constructive technical feedback in code review, design discussions, and 1:1s, and raise standards without demotivating people
  • Grow the team's capability, including how we use AI tooling to work faster without lowering quality

Technical leadership

  • Assess the current engineering bar and raise it. Define what "good" looks like for AI-native development, and make it the shared standard
  • Set and enforce expectations in five areas:
    • Observability: logging, monitoring, and tracing that make AI behavior, cost, and failures visible
    • Testing: strong test coverage and automated-testing rigor, including evaluation of AI outputs
    • Security and compliance: secure-by-default practices, as we move upmarket
    • Scalable architecture and data pipelines: designs that hold up as usage and integrations grow
    • Timeboxing: practical limits on AI development work, so exploration stays bounded and ships
  • Own or steward key architecture decisions, including model selection and integration approach, and the tradeoffs between quality, cost, and latency
  • Flag technical risks early, especially around AI reliability, cost, and edge-case behavior

Hands-on contribution

  • Design, build, and ship AI-powered features alongside the team, from prototyping through production quality
  • Work hands-on with LLMs, embeddings, and related AI tooling to solve real product problems
  • Build across the stack as needed. Every feature you ship should be tested, monitored, and maintainable

Partnership

  • Partner with Product on requirements and priorities, pushing back with technical reality when needed
  • Partner with company leadership on technical planning, resourcing, and sequencing

What You bring to the table

  • Leadership

    • Hands-on technical leadership with real engineering vision. You've led delivery for a small team, ideally for 2-3 years of people leadership, as a tech lead, engineering manager, or player-coach. Formal people-management experience is useful, but the essential need is someone who can wrangle delivery and provide senior technical direction
    • A style that raises the bar. You give direct, specific technical feedback and hold high standards, and the team leaves those conversations more capable and more motivated
    • Delivery discipline. You're comfortable owning timelines, allocating work, and following projects through to the end

    Technical depth

    • 7+ years of software engineering experience, and you've shipped AI features to production and owned the lifecycle from problem framing to post-launch iteration, not just prototypes or AI-assisted coding
    • Strong fullstack fundamentals. Comfortable across frontend, backend, and infrastructure as needed
    • Practical experience with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, RAG, or similar techniques in live systems, with good judgment about when AI is the right tool and when it isn't
    • Observability and testing rigor. You build in logging, monitoring, and tracing from the start, and you insist on strong test coverage and automated testing, including evaluation of AI behavior
    • Scalable architecture and data pipelines. Solid SQL, schema design, and the ability to design pipelines and systems that scale
    • Evaluation mindset. You define success metrics, design experiments, run offline and online evaluations, and make decisions from the results
    • Production readiness. Docker fluency, CI/CD, and good habits for versioning prompts, models, and datasets
    • LLM platform breadth. Experience integrating multiple LLM providers, working with vector databases, and using LangChain (or similar); comfortable fine-tuning when it truly makes sense
    • Security and compliance experience, or a strong interest in it, as we move upmarket
    • Practical timeboxing of AI development work. You know how to keep AI exploration bounded, ship on schedule, and avoid open-ended experimentation

    How you work

    • You identify problems and propose solutions on your own, rather than waiting to be told exactly what to build
    • You're comfortable in a lean team where you own outcomes, not just tickets

What's in it for You

  • Ultimate flexibility: We're 100% remote. You can work from wherever you like, whenever you like.
  • Freedom and autonomy: We're a high-trust team, and you'll be given lots of flexibility to solve problems in your own way — with plenty of help from the team when you need it.

As a Product Manager for Advanced Practice Analytics (APA) within Biopharma Solutions, you will lead the evolution of our premier financial intelligence and reimbursement analytics platform. APA is an enterprise-scale solution designed to deliver insights that optimize specialty practice profitability, formulary selection, and drug purchasing.


Unlike purely clinical platforms, APA is a sophisticated financial engine that delivers critical business insights around specialty formulary management, revenue leakage, buy-and-bill margin optimization, and automated billing reconciliation.


In this role, you will champion an AI-first approach to unlock the value of complex clinical, financial, contract, and claims data. jobs.description:
Keep Growing with Nutrafol

We’re a growing company. Everything we do, we do to help people grow into the best version of themselves. As the pioneers of hair wellness, we create clinically tested products for hair growth and provide support for people at every step of their hair journey.

Our multi-factorial approach targets key root causes of hair thinning using a patented blend of standardized vitamins, minerals and natural ingredients -- and is recommended by over 7,500 physicians and hair professionals for trusted, reliable results. We never settle, and are continuously challenging existing treatments and methodologies to advance the frontier of hair science. As we help our customers grow, we grow too -- by embracing individuality and differences, leading by example, and empowering ourselves and others with our passion for wellness and innovation.

Keep growing. It’s our mantra. Our commitment to helping anybody and everybody committed to realizing their own potential to grow.

About You:

The Director, Brand Marketing, Nutrafol will build and launch the brand story for new product innovations!

Nutrafol is the #1 dermatologist-recommended hair growth supplement brand and the pioneer of the hair wellness category. We’re in the process of developing new product innovation that extends our focus from the inside-out to the outside-in. Your job is to make the range unmistakably Nutrafol - why it exists, who it's for, how it fits the routine she's already in, and why she should believe it works.

You'll set strategy within the Nutrafol masterbrand platform, reporting to the SVP, Brand. You'll partner closely with Product Development, who owns formulation, claims substantiation, and the Unilever R&D and Supply relationship. You bring the consumer into that work: the insight that shapes what we make and the plan that gets it into her hands.

This is a builder's role. You'll start six to twelve months ahead of launch, while formulation is underway and the range is still taking shape - early enough that your read on the consumer changes what we make.

Responsibilities:

Brand and Consumer

  • Own the brand strategy, positioning, and narrative, and make sure it strengthens the Nutrafol masterbrand rather than sitting beside it
  • Hold the deepest understanding of the consumer - where she overlaps with the supplement customer, where she doesn't, and what she's already buying and believing
  • Run the primary and secondary research that answers those questions; turn competitive and category analysis into a point of view, not a deck
  • Identify the insights and tensions that shape both the launch and the next wave of innovation
  • Own naming for the range and individual SKUs, working with Creative, with Legal and Product Development holding sign-off on trademark availability and claims risk

Product Partnership

  • Bring consumer insight and brand POV into the product pipeline - feed the proposition, format, and range decisions that Product Development owns
  • Deliver a ranked consumer-priority claims input ahead of study protocol design, so Product Development and R&D can prioritize what gets tested and substantiated
  • Own how approved claims show up in market — which ones lead, how they're expressed, how they ladder to the story
  • Shape the launch range and wave sequencing as a required consumer input into Product Development's range recommendation
  • Protect the brand across every consumer-facing touchpoint, holding the line on the dermatologist-recommended credibility and the subscription model that built us

Launch and Go-To-Market

  • Build the launch plan across DTC, Amazon, and Pro in partnership with Growth, Marketplaces, CX, and Pro Marketing
  • Accountable for launch readiness and in-market performance against the agreed product availability date, which Product Development owns
  • Own new product innovation pricing above an agreed margin floor set annually with Finance
  • Lead the annual and quarterly brand plan for new product innovation, with clear priorities and a roadmap the cross-functional team can work from
  • Brief and collaborate with Creative; lead ideation on campaign, content, and social narrative
  • Set the brand direction for partnerships, collaborations, and any external voices attached to the range
  • Manage the new product innovation brand marketing budget

Leadership without authority

  • Keep a cross-company group moving to one plan - and know which decisions are yours, which are Product's, and which need both
  • Own the consumer, positioning, and go-to-market sections of Unilever leadership updates, delivered from one shared plan alongside Product Development
  • Give clear, executive-ready updates to Nutrafol leadership
  • Surface risks and dependencies early rather than reporting them after the fact
  • Track performance post-launch and use what you learn to sharpen the range and inform what comes next
  • Build trust fast across teams who've never worked on a launch like this

Requirements:

  • 8–12 years of brand management, brand marketing, or innovation marketing at a high-growth brand; hair care, beauty, or science-led consumer health preferred. DTC experience is required
  • Track record taking a product from concept to market alongside R&D, regulatory, and supply chain - you don't need to have run formulation, but you need to know how to be a good partner to the people who do
  • Proven ability to build integrated brand strategies and launch campaigns across digital, social, CRM, retail media, and direct response
  • Strong commercial and go-to-market instincts across DTC, e-commerce, and omnichannel, including pricing
  • Comfortable at the seam between an entrepreneurial brand and a large matrixed organization, and able to align partners across both without formal authority
  • Fluent in segmentation and in both quantitative and qualitative consumer insight
  • Sharp judgment on claims, positioning, and premium experience
  • Entrepreneurial and self-directed - you'll be hands-on doing the work, not just directing it
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication
  • Low ego, high ownership, and the kind of energy that makes a dispersed team want to be in the room

Shift Paradigm is an execution-led strategic consultancy that bridges the gap between enterprise strategy and technical reality. As partners to the world’s leading MarTech platforms, including Adobe, Salesforce, Optimizely, and Braze, we deploy integrated experts across data analytics, marketing strategy, technology development, engineering, and revenue operations to ensure our clients’ tech stacks don't just exist, but perform.

Location: Remote, US, EST time zone

The Role

As Director of Email Development & QA, you will lead a team of 10-15 developers and QA specialists delivering pixel-perfect campaigns for our Fortune 100 financial services client. You will own the production ecosystem—driving efficiency, automation, and 100% SLA compliance—while collaborating to translate business strategies into scalable technical architectures. This role also involves pre-sale scoping and leading the integration of AI within our workflows.

This role reports directly to our SVP, Managing Director.

Business Leadership and Team Development

Client Delivery and Technical Oversight

Scoping, Resourcing & Burn Management

jobs.description:
Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions that provide reliable power and modernize infrastructure. Since 2000, we have served as a trusted partner to public and private sector customers across North America, the UK and Europe, delivering over $15 billion in solutions and contracting more than 5 GW of energy resources.

At Ameresco, we integrate energy resources and modernize the built environment through innovative infrastructure solutions that improve reliability, optimize performance, strengthen resilience, and support long-term sustainability. Join us in building the infrastructure that powers the future. Explore opportunities to make a meaningful impact while growing your career with a company at the forefront of energy innovation.


Position Overview:

Ameresco is hiring a Senior Project Manager to lead two to three solar PV, distributed generation, community solar, and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects concurrently, depending on project size, phase, and complexity. You will coordinate with Business Development and Preconstruction during project development and turnover, then lead execution from Notice to Proceed through construction, commissioning, commercial operation, and final closeout. The role combines remote project leadership with regular site presence during critical construction, commissioning, and recovery activities and is accountable for safety, schedule, cost, quality, commercial outcomes, and client communication.


This is a hands-on senior project delivery role that combines direct project ownership with cross-functional leadership and mentoring of Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers. This role reports to the Senior Director of Construction – Solar PV & BESS with a preference for candidates located in the Greater Boston area with the ability to work from the Boston office periodically based on business and team needs. Remote U.S. candidates may be considered for the right fit and will be expected to travel to the Boston office quarterly.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner with Business Development and Preconstruction to review contract requirements, estimate assumptions, baseline schedules, procurement, permitting, interconnection, constructability, site logistics, staffing, and subcontractor strategy, then convert the sold project into an executable plan with clear scope, budget, schedule, risk ownership, and decision paths before mobilization.
  • Lead assigned solar PV, distributed generation, community solar, and BESS projects from Notice to Proceed through commercial operation and final closeout.
  • Manage procurement and subcontractor performance, including scope alignment, commitments, deliverables, schedule compliance, field coordination, and issue resolution.
  • Direct cross-functional project teams that include Construction Managers, Superintendents, Engineering, Procurement, Safety, Quality, project controls, subcontractors, OEMs, and support staff.
  • Manage project budgets, forecasts, contingency, cash flow, and margin, and drive value-engineering opportunities with Engineering and Procurement.
  • Lead project-level change-order development, negotiation, claims support, schedule recovery, and management of liquidated-damages exposure; escalate material commercial and contractual risks to Commercial, Legal, and senior leadership.
  • Maintain the baseline schedule, evaluate critical-path impacts, develop recovery plans, and hold internal teams and contractors accountable for commitments.
  • Serve as the primary day-to-day client contact, coordinate with utilities and developers, communicate decisions and risks clearly, and resolve or escalate issues before they affect project outcomes.
  • Coordinate testing, commissioning, energization, turnover, and applicable BESS, electrical, fire-code, permitting, prevailing-wage, apprenticeship, and certified-payroll requirements with the responsible internal teams, OEMs, consultants, utilities, and authorities having jurisdiction.
  • Drive commercial operation and final closeout, including punch-list completion, documentation, training, warranties, final account reconciliation, and resolution of remaining exposure.
  • Provide accurate, decision-ready project reporting to the Senior Director of Construction, including safety, cost, schedule, procurement, quality, commercial exposure, key decisions, and required support.
  • Mentor Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers, reinforce consistent project controls, and share practical lessons learned across the construction team.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant construction experience.
  • Minimum of 10 years of construction project management experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years supporting solar PV, BESS, distributed generation, community solar, or related power infrastructure projects.
  • Experience managing projects valued from $5M to $150M+.
  • Strong command of EPC/EPCM delivery, subcontract management, and construction execution.
  • Proven commercial skills: change-order negotiation, claims management, and cost forecasting.
  • Experience leading or mentoring project managers.
  • Proven ability to manage projects, teams, and contractors remotely, with strong written communication.
  • Willingness to travel 20–30% to assigned project sites; valid driver's license required.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Direct utility-scale solar construction experience, including project execution through commissioning and closeout.
  • Utility-scale BESS construction and commissioning experience, including OEM coordination and energization.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 855, UL 9540/9540A, NFPA 70E, and NEC, with AHJ/fire-department permitting experience.
  • Experience with applicable IRA prevailing-wage and apprenticeship requirements, including certified-payroll documentation.
  • Utility interconnection experience (e.g., ISO-NE, PJM, MISO).
  • PMP and/or PE; OSHA 30; NABCEP a plus.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Project, Procore, and other construction management software.

Meet Aperture

At Aperture, we create value and drive growth by delivering exceptional product consultancy and advertising services to our global partners.

Through data-driven strategies, we combine performance marketing, creative strategy, product optimisation, CRM, analytics and experimentation to help ambitious companies scale.

Founded in 2022 by Hannah Parvaz, Aperture has quickly made waves. Already recognised as Business Consultant of the Year and named 2024’s Most Innovative Growth Agency, we’re now building the team that will take us into our next stage of growth.

We work with some of the most exciting apps, platforms and digital products in the world. Our job is not just to make things look good. Our job is to make growth happen.

Our culture

  • Growth mindset. We’re hungry to learn and improve.
  • Take full responsibility for every outcome. No excuses.
  • Obsess over results. We’re here to make a measurable impact.
  • We’re data-obsessed. We let numbers, not opinions, guide our decisions.
  • Client success is our success. Period.
  • No ego. The best idea wins, regardless of who it comes from.
  • Radical candour. We give and receive honest feedback to fuel growth.
  • No job is too small. We support each other and JFDI.

Work from anywhere

We’re remote-first and impact-first.

Work from wherever you’re most productive, while staying closely connected to the team through regular collaboration, team sessions, client work and in-person meetups.

We also bring the team together for retreats, events, conferences and working sessions around the world. Travel to team meetups is covered.

You must be able to work in a UK timezone.

The role

We’re hiring a Video Editor to create brilliant, high-performing content for our clients and Aperture.

You should be chronically online, in the best possible way.

You know what people are watching, sharing and talking about. You spot emerging formats before every brand starts copying them. You understand why a video holds someone’s attention, when an edit feels native and when something feels too polished, too slow or painfully corporate.

You’ll turn raw footage, creator content, product recordings, AI-generated assets and creative concepts into paid social ads and organic content that people actually want to watch.

AI-native. Human-led.

This is an AI-native creative role, but it is fundamentally human-led.

We're not looking for people who can generate content. We're looking for tastemakers: editors with exceptional judgement who know what feels fresh, what feels native and what people actually want to watch.

AI expands what's possible, but taste is what makes the work valuable. The tools will keep changing; your eye for storytelling, internet culture, pacing and creative direction is what sets the standard.

If you're the person sending references before everyone else has seen them, spotting formats before they become trends, and pushing ideas beyond the obvious, you'll fit right in.

Requirements

What you’ll do

  • Edit paid social ads, UGC, creator content and short-form organic videos.
  • Turn raw footage into compelling stories with strong hooks, pacing and structure.
  • Create multiple versions of concepts to test different openings, messages, formats and lengths.
  • Add captions, music, sound design, graphics, transitions and motion where they improve the work.
  • Adapt videos for TikTok, Reels, Meta, YouTube Shorts and emerging platforms.
  • Use generative video, image, voice and audio tools to create, transform and extend creative assets.
  • Combine AI-generated scenes with creator footage, product recordings, motion graphics and traditional edits.
  • Experiment with tools such as Luma, Runway, Kling, Veo and whatever emerges next.
  • Develop repeatable AI workflows that increase the speed, range and ambition of our creative output.
  • Keep up with trends, creators, sounds, memes, editing styles and wider internet culture.
  • Bring relevant references and proactive ideas into creative discussions.
  • Work closely with creative strategists, designers, performance marketers and creator managers.
  • Use performance results to improve future edits and iterate on winning ideas.
  • Share new tools, techniques and creative possibilities with the wider team.
  • Keep projects, source files and versions organised across multiple accounts.

You’ll be great at this if

  • You have a strong portfolio of short-form video work.
  • You understand how to earn attention within the first few seconds.
  • You have an instinct for pacing, storytelling, humour, tension and timing.
  • You can edit quickly without the work feeling careless.
  • You understand the visual language of TikTok, Instagram, Meta and YouTube.
  • You know the difference between using a trend well and arriving after it is already dead.
  • You’re confident using Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut or similar tools.
  • You’re already experimenting with AI creative tools and can show us what you’ve made.
  • You understand that prompting is only one part of the process; taste, direction, editing and iteration are what make the output good.
  • You can recognise and correct the inconsistencies, artefacts and visual clichés that make AI-generated content feel cheap.
  • You’re excited by how quickly creative technology is changing and actively teach yourself new workflows.
  • You can take inconsistent or imperfect footage and find the strongest possible edit.
  • You take feedback well, move quickly and aren’t precious about your work.
  • You care about how your work performs, not just how it looks.

Experience editing performance ads, UGC or creator-led content is a strong advantage, but exceptional social-first work matters more than a particular background.

This is not the role for you if

  • You don’t spend much time on social platforms.
  • You only want to work on polished brand films or long-form productions.
  • You need every shot and transition mapped out before you can begin.
  • You prefer perfecting one video to producing and testing multiple strong versions.
  • You’re interested in making beautiful videos but not whether people watch or act on them.
  • You have no interest in using AI as part of your creative process.
  • You treat AI as a shortcut for weak ideas, poor craft or generic content.
  • You’re uncomfortable receiving frequent, direct feedback.

What success looks like in six months

  • Our videos feel current, native and distinctive.
  • Strong concepts are being turned into multiple testable edits quickly.
  • Winning hooks, structures and formats are being identified and iterated.
  • Editing is increasing the speed and quality of our creative output.
  • AI is meaningfully increasing the range and ambition of what we produce without reducing its quality.
  • You have introduced repeatable AI-assisted workflows that the wider creative team can use.
  • Performance learnings are consistently influencing new work.
  • The team trusts you to bring ideas, spot opportunities and deliver excellent work.

Benefits

  • Work from anywhere, with flexibility around how you structure your day.
  • Direct exposure to high-growth clients and meaningful work.
  • Regular team meetups and retreats, with travel covered.
  • Access to conferences, events and industry sessions.
  • Small team, high ownership and fast progression.

Before you apply

We read every application.

Show us the work that best represents your editing style, particularly short-form content, paid social, UGC or creator-led videos. Include anything you have created or enhanced using AI.

If you haven’t yet used AI extensively, tell us what you’re experimenting with and what you would be excited to create.

We’ll also ask a few questions about what you’re watching, what you think is working and how you approach an edit.

Specific, honest answers matter far more than polished ones. We can tell when something is generic.

About the team

Studio Z is Zillow's in-house creative agency — a full-service creative, content, strategy, and production team that drives Zillow's brand forward across every channel while operating at the high-stakes intersection of brand storytelling and real-time culture. The team is small, highly skilled, and deeply collaborative — working alongside copywriters, art directors, and brand partners to make content that earns attention rather than buying it. They move at the speed of social, obsess over platform nuance, and build work that immerses the Zillow brand in culture. This is a team for people who take the internet seriously and love the craft of creating for it.

About the role

We are looking for an inventive, high-execution hybrid Creator & Strategist who lives at the intersection of culture, community, and short-form storytellers. You are equally comfortable behind the camera concepting and editing, and in front of the camera as an authentic face and voice for the Zillow brand.

In this role within StudioZ (Zillow’s in-house creative organization), you will help bring Zillow’s overarching social strategy to life across our key channels. Working in close partnership with internal Line-of-Business (LOB) leads and our external creative agency partners, you know how to navigate a collaborative, matrixed environment to deliver work that is timely, additive, and culturally resonant. You bring quick-thinking creative instincts, respect established brand guardrails, and solve complex production challenges with agility and taste.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategic & Agile Content Creation: Concept, script, shoot, and edit platform-native short-form content quickly—applying proven workflows, agile production techniques, and modern creative tools to turn real-time cultural moments into compelling brand creative.
  • Brand Representation: Serve as a confident, authentic, and charismatic voice and storyteller for Zillow social and real-time trend responses.
  • Cross-Functional & Agency Collaboration: Partner seamlessly across StudioZ (internal creative agency), internal lines of business creative leads, Social, PR, and external agency partners. Respect established brand platforms and workflows while bringing fresh, expert executions that elevate the collective work.
  • Cultural Listening & Audience Acumen: Monitor digital subcultures, platform trends, and real-time conversation to identify strategic opportunities for Zillow to participate with low friction, high taste, and deep audience understanding.
  • Recurring Series Iteration: Contribute to and iterate on recurring social formats, helping translate overarching brand narratives and product truths into engaging, long-term audience moments.
  • Brand Governance & Approvals: Navigate approvals across Legal, Brand, and Production efficiently—ensuring fast-moving social work stays on-brand, compliant, and aligned with core business priorities.
  • Platform Mastery: Maintain deep fluency across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and emerging platforms—understanding shifting algorithms, tone, and audience behaviors in real time.

Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

Who You Are

  • 3–5+ years of experience creating social-first content for major brands, media platforms, or an established personal channel with a proven track record of driving meaningful engagement.
  • End-to-End Creator Craft: Mastery of short-form video production (writing, shooting, lighting, editing) paired with high taste and strong creative judgment.
  • Collaborative Partner Mindset: A low-ego, highly collaborative team player who excels in a matrixed workplace—knowing how to check ego at the door, partner across teams, and execute against shared brand goals.
  • On-Camera Comfort: Natural camera presence, charismatic storytelling ability, and the skill to communicate complex brand/product truths in a relatable, human way.

As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. jobs.excerpt: Civica builds software that runs essential public services.
jobs.description:
Civica builds software that runs essential public services. Our systems support local government, the NHS, housing associations, and financial institutions - services that millions of people depend on every day. When our software works well, caseworkers make better decisions, clinicians access the right information, and councils deliver services that communities rely on.

We're not a startup chasing the next hype cycle. We're a company with deep roots in the public sector, working on problems that matter - and we're investing seriously in how we build software to make sure we can keep doing that for the next decade.

Why you will love this opportunity as Senior Software Engineer at Civica

We're hiring Senior Software Engineers to work on business-critical products across our portfolio. You'll be embedded in a product team, working across legacy and greenfield environments, translating ambiguous business problems into production-grade solutions.

We care about engineering judgement - the ability to decompose hard problems, design systems that last, and ship software that works in production. We expect you to use modern tooling, including AI-assisted development, as part of how you work. But the signal we're hiring on is your thinking, not your toolset.

You'll work on systems with real users, real constraints, and real consequences. Some of that work will be modernising legacy codebases that have served public services for years. Some will be building new capabilities from scratch. All of it requires someone who thinks in systems, not just code.

Responsibilities:

  • Decompose ambiguous problems into clear system designs, making architectural decisions that balance immediate needs with long-term maintainability
  • Design, build, and ship production-ready software across the full lifecycle. From specification through to deployment and operability
  • Work across mixed environments - legacy modernisation alongside greenfield development, often within the same product
  • Own technical decisions for complex system components, articulating trade-offs in terms your product manager and your principal engineer both understand
  • Define what "good" looks like for your area of the codebase - testing strategy, code quality, observability, and documentation
  • Collaborate with product, design, and other engineers to understand the real problem before building anything

Requirements

  • A track record of building and shipping complex, real-world software systems - not just contributing to large codebases, but owning meaningful pieces end-to-end
  • System design and architectural reasoning - you think about how components interact, where the failure modes are, and what happens at boundaries
  • Problem decomposition under ambiguity - you ask 'why' before 'how' and can translate a vague business need into a structured technical approach
  • Production-quality discipline - you care about testing, observability, error handling, and operational readiness, not just making things work locally
  • Communication that reaches beyond engineers - you can explain a technical trade-off to a product manager, write a clear specification, and build consensus on contentious decisions
  • Learning agility - you pick up new stacks, tools, and domains quickly. You've worked across more than one language or framework and you're comfortable in unfamiliar territory
  • Ownership and initiative - you identify problems before they're assigned to you and follow through until they're resolved in production

Nice to have

  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, or similar) as part of your daily workflow
  • Comfort evaluating and validating AI-generated code to the same standard as human-written code
  • Experience in the public sector, health, housing, or local government domains
  • Familiarity with .NET, Go, React/TypeScript, or similar modern stacks - we're polyglot, so language-specific depth matters less than the ability to learn
  • Experience with legacy modernisation - understanding the constraints, risks, and stakeholder dynamics of replacing systems that are still in production
  • Exposure to platform or product-led engineering environments

Benefits

Why You'll Love Working with Us
As a company, we're passionate about what we do and the citizens we serve. If you, too, want to champion the use of technology in public services to improve outcomes for citizens and public sector organizations, then Civica is the right place for you. We will help you unlock the best version of yourself, achieve career growth, and make a real difference to people and communities.

We know that when our people are happy, they work better and have greater job satisfaction. Here's what you can expect:

✔ 25 Days Annual Leave + bank holidays – plus the option to buy up to 10 extra days!
✔ Days of Difference – Up to 3 extra days off for volunteering.

✔ Income Protection – Up to 75% salary cover for long-term illness.
✔ Life Assurance – 4x salary tax-free lump sum.
✔ Critical Illness Cover – £25,000 lump sum (extendable to dependents).

Health & Perks

✔ Private Medical Insurance – Fast access to private healthcare.
✔ Health Cash Plan – Claim back physio, therapies & more.
✔ Dental Insurance – Cover for routine & emergency care.
✔ Affinity Groups – Join employee-led communities.
✔ Bounty Bonus – Refer a friend & get rewarded.

About Kyra

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

💡 The role in a nutshell

You own a portfolio of Kyra's largest enterprise accounts (multi-million-dollar brand partnerships) and you're measured on whether they grow. Retention, expansion, and Net Revenue Retention are your scoreboard.

💡 What You'll Own

This is a commercial role, not a delivery one. You keep enterprise clients, grow them, and run delivery cleanly enough that growth is never at risk.

  • Revenue. You carry an NRR target across your book. You protect it, and you grow it.

  • The relationship. You're the trusted strategic partner to senior brand-side stakeholders, not the campaign contact.

  • The system. You're the connective tissue between Sales, Strategy, Campaigns, Paid, and Product, and you keep them aligned and operating efficiently.

  • The early warning. When something drifts (performance, scope, relationship, or margin) you see it two quarters out and fix it before it becomes a problem. No surprises. No scrambling. Just steady, commercial ownership.

  • The standard. You lead a pod of CSMs and/or Junior CSMs. Their performance and their client work is yours to elevate.

🎯 Lead the Relationship

Own client relationships across launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on programs. Multi-thread across teams. Build trust. Have direct conversations when performance needs to improve.

📈 Turn Insight into Strategy

Translate data into clear, actionable plans. Present performance against KPIs (engagement, EMV, sales lift, affiliate impact) and explain what it means.

🤖 AI-First
You'll be expected to use AI daily to compress reporting, model renewals, prep upsells, and synthesise client data, so you can buy back time for the things that add value, like managing the relationship.

🔍 Own Delivery End-to-End

Manage timelines, scopes, budgets, and execution across seeding, paid, and integrated campaigns. Keep work on-brand, on-time, and within margin.

📊 Protect & Grow Revenue

Manage renewal timelines. Identify upsell opportunities. Drive Net Revenue Retention. Be able to speak confidently about account growth with real numbers.

💾 Use Data to Improve What's Next

Forecast performance. Optimise mid-campaign. Apply learnings to the next program. Reporting informs decisions; it's not a recap.

🛡️ Keep the System Tight

Keep tracking clean. Watch team capacity. Fix what's inefficient. Make sure client feedback doesn't get lost.

What We're Looking For

  • We're looking for someone who has:

  • 6+ years in influencer or creator marketing, with real time on large or enterprise accounts

  • Hands-on campaign fluency, with genuine command of Meta and TikTok

  • A track record of account growth and retention you can quantify, so bring the numbers

  • You've been measured against revenue, retention, or NRR before, and you know what moved them

  • Direct people-leadership experience. You've run 1:1s, managed workload, and lifted the performance of people you're responsible for

  • AI-native. You build AI tools into your daily work for faster execution, sharper insight, and smarter workflows

  • You should be commercially sharp, operationally reliable, and able to speak confidently about the revenue impact of the accounts you've managed.

Traits That Matter

Curious. Commercially aware. Direct. Adaptable. Strong at building trust. Open to feedback. You don't avoid hard conversations. You don't wait for issues to escalate. You don't need constant direction.

What Success Looks Like

6 months in: renewals are planned early, NRR targets are on track, expansion opportunities are clearly mapped, delivery runs smoothly, and leadership trusts your forecast.

Benefits

🌎 Remote-first, so you can work from wherever you do your best work
🌴 Annual Time Off: 25 days PTO + bank holidays, 4 company-wide days off (Kyra Days), 3 wellness days, and paid sick leave each year
📚 Growth: Annual Learning & Development budget to invest in your skills
💰 Rewards: Annual bonus scheme to recognise great work
🩺 Healthcare coverage for US-based team members

👉 Tips for Application

AI is core to how we operate. Use it to elevate your work. But everything in your application should reflect your own judgement and experience.

💟 Support

If you have a condition or require an adjustment to our interview process - please let us know so we can make adjustments to support you. Please note that when you submit an application or resume, your data will be processed in line with our privacy policy.

Compensation Range: $100K - $110K

Qualifications/Competencies/Skills

jobs.description:
Job Description

NetImpact Strategies builds software for Federal agencies, and we build it with AI. We are hiring engineers who own a solution end to end: sit with the customer, turn what they need into a specification, direct AI coding agents to build it, prove it works, get it into a Federal production environment, and hand it to sustainment. You will work in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and our proprietary AI software generation platform every day.

The Technical Architect extracts meaning from what a customer is asking and converts it into the right technology. The role is senior enough to own the architecture, close enough to the customer to understand the intent behind a request, and accountable when the solution goes live. The Core functions of the role are Research, Design, Architect, Code with AI, Solution Validation, and discipline to be productive with Client intimacy.

What makes the role different

This is not a conventional architect who designs and hands off, a people manager, or a quota-carrying salesperson. AI generation changes how code is produced, but it does not transfer accountability: production code ships under this role’s ownership.

Responsibilities

  • Participate directly in requirements capture, translate customer needs into fit-for-purpose solutions, and define the technical scope and boundaries for fixed-price engagements.
  • Convert customer requirements into structured specifications, acceptance criteria, and architectural decisions that enable AI-assisted software development, while validating generated solutions before release.
  • Lead production integration, guide deployments, and remain accountable through deployment, stabilization, customer acceptance, and knowledge transfer to ensure successful delivery.
  • Ensure solutions are extensible, maintainable, and transferable so they can be supported and enhanced by other qualified team members.
  • Deliver production-ready solutions by supporting cloud deployments, CI/CD, legacy system integration, and compliance with ATO/RMF, Section 508, and NIST requirements.
  • Create reusable assets, share lessons learned across the organization, and identify opportunities for follow-on work while transitioning commercial activities to the appropriate stakeholders.

Qualifications

Required qualifications

  • Demonstrate a strong foundation in software engineering principles and manual coding, with the ability to architect and deliver solutions across modern programming languages, frameworks, cloud platforms, AI-assisted development tools, and low-code platforms.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.6+ years of professional software delivery, including enterprise systems you carried into production and supported after go-live.
  • A complete solution built primarily with agentic AI coding tools. At least one working, end-to-end application you built by directing Claude Code, Codex, Copilot agent mode, Cursor, or an equivalent tool. Work or substantive personal projects both count. You will be asked to show it and to build live during the interview.
  • Enterprise delivery experience. Demonstrated ownership of enterprise-scale software delivery, including production integration, deployment, operational constraints, and post-launch stabilization.
  • Architect-level depth. Strong systems-design judgment plus working fluency across analysis, product ownership, software development, project delivery, security, data, integrations, and operations.
  • AI-directed solution delivery. Evidence of independently building complete working solutions primarily through AI-assisted generation. Substantive personal projects may demonstrate this capability.
  • Generated-code verification. Ability to read unfamiliar generated logic, identify failure modes, design appropriate tests, and determine whether the system is safe and correct enough to ship.Technology breadth. Ability to compare and select technologies based on context rather than defaulting to a familiar stack.
  • Customer and contextual judgment. Ability to uncover the meaning behind stated requirements, read stakeholders, and adapt the approach to the engagement’s real constraints.
  • Problem solving and persistence. A record of making progress through ambiguity, obstacles, incomplete information, and cross-organizational dependency.
  • Software-delivery orientation. Hands-on experience must be primarily in delivering software solutions rather than infrastructure or operations alone.Willingness and demonstrated ability to work across greenfield builds, modernization, integration-heavy environments, and inherited in-flight work.
  • Full-stack fluency across the environments above, with production experience in at least one .NET or Java enterprise ecosystem and at least one major cloud.
  • Verification mindset. You define acceptance criteria, design test strategies, use automated testing, and instrument systems so behavior can be observed. You treat "the agent said it works" as the start of verification, not the end.
  • Customer-facing communication. You can run a discovery session, demo to a skeptical stakeholder, and explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical program owner.
  • US citizenship and eligibility for a Secret clearance.

This role is probably not for you if:

  • You want to design the system and let someone else build it.
  • You want to be handed a design and build exactly that.
  • You use AI coding tools as autocomplete and prefer to write the code yourself.
  • You need a single familiar stack to be productive.
  • You would rather not demo to a customer, or hear from one that the first version missed.

About Us

At NetImpact Strategies, we post salary ranges in compliance with the specific labor laws and regulations of each county and state, ensuring transparency and fairness in our hiring practices. This approach reflects our commitment to adhering to legal requirements and promoting equitable pay standards across all regions where we operate. The posted salary range for this role is $170,000-210,000. The posted salary range is not an exact indication of the actual compensation offered and is instead a range of what NetImpact, in good faith, could compensate at the lowest and most high end of the salary market. In general, NetImpact may not pay the top of the salary range. Compensations are determined by several mitigating factors including skillset, experience, trainings, location, and other factors including benefits packages.

Perks of working at NetImpact Strategies

  • Invest in your future – 401(k) Plan – Immediately vested employer contributions; no matching required
  • Work hard, play hard – we offer a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) policy, one (1) additional day of paid wellness leave per calendar year, and observe ten (10) federal holidays
  • Pawsitively pawesome – Pet Insurance (because our little critters are part of our families, too!)

Overview

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Software Developer’s primary role is designing, developing, testing, and deploying end-to-end software applications and automations. This role works closely with the Software Architect and Platform Development Manager to support various programming and scripting languages that are deployed across various environments, both in Azure and a traditional datacenter. The Software Developer is also responsible for maintaining, enhancing, and troubleshooting legacy applications. Additionally, this position collaborates with the data science team, platform automation team, and other various business units.

The base pay estimate for this role is $66,900-$113,700 annually. The final offer will depend on the skills, experience, and qualifications of the selected candidate. This range is for base pay only and does not include bonuses or other compensation. This position is eligible for an annual bonus. Bonuses are not guaranteed and are awarded based on company and individual performance.

Job Highlights

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: (The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation): pineapple

  • Develops, maintains, and troubleshoots web and mobile applications.
  • Develops, maintains, and troubleshoots automations and scripts across various languages such as .NET, C#, and Python.
  • Writes clean, maintainable, and well-documented code by following documented frameworks.
  • Participates in code reviews and contributes to team knowledge sharing.
  • Debugs and troubleshoots software and script issues. Performs root cause analysis in complex applications.
  • Collaborates with designers, developers, and product managers to implement new features.
  • Tests and deploys applications, scripts, and cloud-based technologies.
  • Stays up to date with emerging trends and technologies. Stays current with industry standards by studying state-of-the-art development tools and programming techniques; participates in educational opportunities; reads professional publications.
  • Protects operations and maintains HIPAA compliance by keeping information confidential and working within specific guidelines.
  • Collaborates respectfully with other team members.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES (KSAs):

  • Bachelor’s degree in an appropriate field of study and 3+ years of experience as a software developer.
  • 3+ years of experience performing root cause analysis and other troubleshooting methodologies.
  • Full understanding of Well Architected Frameworks.
  • 3+ years of experience with functional, imperative, and object-oriented languages (knowledge of C# and Java is preferred).
  • 1 year of experience with scripting languages such as Python.
  • Experience with Azure based microservices and infrastructure.
  • Experience coding, testing, and documenting complex systems.
  • Ability to use version control software such as GIT.
  • Experience communicating with users, other technical teams, and management to collect requirements, identify tasks, provide estimates, and meet production deadlines.
  • Experience with professional software engineering best practices for the full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations.
  • Experience with unit test methodologies.
  • 2+ years of experience with SQL Server or Azure SQL.
  • 2+ years of experience working with Azure DevOps as a code repository/task tracking and leveraging automated tests, CI builds, and release pipelines.
  • The ability to work efficiently on multiple projects simultaneously.
  • The ability to apply the Azure Well Architected Framework to all designs, troubleshooting, and deployments.
  • The ability to learn quickly across various technologies and programming languages.
  • The ability to work through complex problems in a structured manner.
  • The ability to work in an Agile software development environment and work within a Scrum team.

  • Occasional Walking

Overview

Technical Services Engineer

Location: Remote (US)Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent

About HealthEdge

HealthEdge delivers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance organizations, enabling health plans to modernize operations, improve performance, and maintain a competitive advantage in a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape. As we continue to grow, we're investing in the talent that drives our success and shapes the future of healthcare technology.

Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

Position Overview

The Technical Service Engineer serves as a senior technical support resource responsible for advanced application support, incident management, root cause analysis, and resolution of complex production issues within the GuidingCare platform. This role acts as a critical bridge between Level 1 Support, Engineering, Product, and Infrastructure teams to ensure exceptional system availability, operational stability, and customer satisfaction.

Key Responsibilities:

Production Support & Incident Management

  • Monitor, triage, and resolve production incidents across all severity levels.
  • Meet established SLA response and resolution targets.
  • Perform real-time incident analysis and communicate status updates to customers and stakeholders.
  • Coordinate emergency production fixes and hotfix deployments with Engineering and Infrastructure teams.
  • Serve as the primary escalation point for complex issues from L1 Support.

Root Cause Analysis & Troubleshooting

  • Investigate and resolve critical and high-priority production incidents.
  • Conduct detailed root cause analyses using logs, auditing data, and system diagnostics.
  • Troubleshoot issues across application, database, and configuration layers.
  • Analyze application logs, stack traces, and error reports to identify defects.
  • Document findings and provide detailed technical recommendations to Product and Development teams.

Database & Data Operations

  • Write and execute complex SQL/T-SQL queries for troubleshooting and analysis.
  • Perform backend data corrections, updates, migrations, and cleanup activities.
  • Support change management processes, including CAB approvals and production data fixes.
  • Validate and maintain data integrity across environments.

Application & Configuration Management

  • Support customer configurations across QA, UAT, Training, and Production environments.
  • Manage configuration synchronizations and GUID consistency between environments.
  • Resolve configuration and synchronization failures.
  • Administer user provisioning, access controls, and role-based permissions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Product, Development, Infrastructure, DBA, DevOps, and Customer-Facing teams to resolve issues.
  • Prepare detailed escalation packages, including investigation results and technical findings.
  • Drive resolution efforts while minimizing escalation turnaround times.
  • Participate in customer calls for issue verification and resolution discussions.

Customer Communication

  • Act as a direct technical contact for enterprise customers.
  • Provide timely, professional communication regarding incidents and resolutions.
  • Develop customer-facing summaries and technical updates.
  • Support demonstrations, validations, and issue review meetings.

Process Improvement & Automation

  • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive support activities.
  • Develop scripts and tools to streamline support and data correction processes.
  • Implement process improvements that reduce ticket volume and increase efficiency.
  • Build proactive monitoring and alerting capabilities.

Core Technologies

  • SQL Server / T-SQL
  • C# / .NET Framework / .NET Core
  • ASP.NET Core
  • REST APIs and SOAP Web Services
  • SSIS
  • SQL Server Agent
  • IIS / Windows Server

Support & Operations Tools

  • Application Log Analysis
  • Jira
  • ServiceNow
  • Confluence
  • Git / Source Control

Preferred Qualifications:

  • AWS and/or Azure Cloud Platforms
  • Python or Bash scripting
  • Docker and Kubernetes
  • Active Directory / LDAP
  • Dynatrace or AppDynamics
  • Experience supporting healthcare technology applications

Required Experience:

  • 4–6 years of experience supporting enterprise software applications in a Technical Support, Production Support, or Technical Services environment.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex production issues across application and database layers.
  • Strong SQL development and data analysis experience.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Industry Knowledge:

  • Healthcare IT experience strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with payer, care management, or healthcare administration platforms is a plus.

Core Competencies:

  • Problem Solving
  • Ownership & Accountability
  • Communication Skills
  • Attention to Detail
  • Customer Focus
  • Collaboration
  • Leadership
  • Process Improvement
  • Continuous Learning
  • Ability to Perform Under Pressure

Bachelor's degree in one of the following preferred fields:

  • Computer Science

  • Healthcare Informatics
  • Related technical discipline
